title: Reαd carefully: how to spot – and avoid – a homoglyph attack
author: Hilary Osborne
content:
You’ve read the email carefully and it looks legitimate. The link it asks you to click on has none of the usual red flags: there are no weird numbers or extra parts to the URL. You feel safe to proceed.
But if you had looked slightly closer you may have noticed something slightly wrong with one of the characters. Just as in the headline of this piece where instead of “a” we used the Cyrillic “α”.
Fraudsters can use letters from different alphabets to create URLs and email addresses that look almost identical to the real thing, but in reality send anyone who clicks on them to a spoof website or inbox. From there they can harvest personal details to use in their scams.
There are other letters and symbols that are easily switched. Last year tech experts spotted fraudsters using the Japanese hiragana character ん to look like a / in an address designed to look as though it was on Booking.com’s website.
Jake Moore, global security adviser at cybersecurity company ESET, says the fraudsters “love Microsoft” as a company identity to spoof. “A fake site might use the Cyrillic “с” instead of the Latin “c” (miсrosoft v microsoft),” he says.
![a hand presses a button a darkened laptop keyboard](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/72734997bddd9bb5ed4870c43532f6ecb0f2c2aa/83_0_3967_3174/master/3967.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Moore says this type of fraud – known as a homoglyph attack – is becoming increasingly popular. A homoglyph is a character that looks very similar, or even identical, to another one.
“Most phishing attacks are designed to point people to links these days instead of downloading attachments. Attachments can easily be scanned and caught by security software if malicious,” he says.
“Therefore, criminals need to design their websites where the links look genuine and casually request people to click on them without thinking.”
Marijus Briedis, chief technology officer at NordVPN, says homoglyph attacks “are really more of a psychological trick than a technical one”, because the fraudsters are typically trying to panic you into responding quickly, rather than taking time to check things out.
“The goal is to create a sense of panic so you don’t look too closely at the URL. They’re betting that when we’re in a rush, our brains see what we expect to see,” Briedis says.
 It just goes to show that the split-second decision you make when clicking a link is often the most vulnerable part of the whole security chain.”
What it looks like
The real thing. Until you look closely.
You will receive an email or text message suggesting you need to click on a URL or email to sort something out.
![a speech bubble emanates from a smartphone asking for you to click through a link](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/38ae61991009d50c9d77bb0071f4b0817e70688e/0_0_4811_2706/master/4811.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Some fonts make substitutions almost impossible to detect. In an email address given in comic sans , for example, the Cyrillic a does not look at all out of place.
“We’ve spent years telling people to check the website before trusting it but the problem with this technique is that you can do exactly that and still be fooled as it can look as it should,” says Moore.
If it’s a URL, Moore says typically it will lead to a site that encourages you to enter your credentials for the real site, including your username, password and even a one-time passcode.
What to do
If you are sent a link, take a moment to think rather than reacting immediately.
“If any text, WhatsApp or email is asking you to log in anywhere, it is vital that you independently visit the genuine website rather than trusting the link in front of you to save a few seconds,” says Moore.
And apply the same thinking to email addresses. Type in the address you know to be correct, rather than clicking on a link.
Keep your browser updated. It will flag up suspicious websites, and by keeping it updated it will catch the criminals’ latest workarounds.
Put in place two-factor authentication, or multifactor authentication (2FA or MFA), which means you have two steps to log into a site.
If you find that your details have been compromised, change your passwords immediately. Contact your bank and report the phishing attack to Report Fraud.
summary: Homoglyph attacks involve fraudsters using characters from different alphabets to create deceptive URLs and email addresses that look legitimate. These attacks rely on psychological tricks like panic to prevent victims from noticing subtle character substitutions. Experts recommend avoiding links in unsolicited messages, visiting official websites independently, keeping browsers updated, and using multi-factor authentication.
key_points: Fraudsters use lookalike characters from alphabets like Cyrillic or Japanese hiragana to spoof trusted websites and email addresses.
Homoglyph attacks rely on psychological pressure to create panic so victims do not closely inspect URLs.
Fake sites often direct users to pages designed to harvest credentials, usernames, passwords, and one-time passcodes.
Security experts advise independently navigating to genuine websites rather than clicking links in texts, WhatsApp, or emails.
Protective measures include keeping browsers updated, using multi-factor authentication, and changing passwords immediately if compromised.

title: Top Stories: iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate Out Now, Siri AI Waitlist, and More
author: MacRumors Staff
content:
All of Apple's products introduced at last week's event with the exception of the iPhone Duo are now available, with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5 all launching on Friday.
![top stories 2026 09 19](https://images.macrumors.com/t/lxqUeOu8E4fB9mFgJSvyzcLiSMY=/400x0/article-new/2026/09/top-stories-2026-09-19.jpg?lossy)
While new hardware is always a welcome arrival, users of existing hardware also got big upgrades this week with the releases of iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate and more. Apple is also already looking ahead to iOS 27.1 that will ship with the iPhone Duo next month and iOS 27.2 that will see the first significant round of improvements to iOS 27 for all users, so read on below for all of details on these stories and more!
Top Stories
Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 With Siri AI and Liquid Glass Update
Following last week's big iPhone event, this week saw the traditional public release of Apple's new major operating system updates, headlined by iOS 27 and iPadOS 27.
![iOS 27 Out Now Thumb](https://images.macrumors.com/t/_-5Ce3cNU8cxNkCu6A7wV0AW7qE=/400x0/article-new/2026/09/iOS-27-Out-Now-Thumb.jpg?lossy)
iOS 27 brings new Siri AI capabilities to users in many countries around the world, as well as a variety of other new features and improvements. For a quick introduction to iOS 27, check out our list of 10 features to try first, and when you're ready for more, move on to our look at 50 new things your iPhone can do in iOS 27.
And for the most thorough look at what's new, our iOS 27 Ultimate Mega Guide links to all of the feature coverage we've been putting together for the release.
macOS Golden Gate Now Available With Siri AI, Visual Intelligence and More
On the Mac side, this week saw the release of macOS Golden Gate 27. The update introduces Siri AI, a smarter chatbot version of Siri with a dedicated Siri app. It also brings Visual Intelligence to the Mac for the first time, and tweaks the look of the Liquid Glass design update Apple introduced last year.
![macOS 27 next to MacBook Pro Running macOS 27](https://images.macrumors.com/t/opoIXXSfQcIPqUsSt1LDCg7P3jw=/400x0/article-new/2026/06/macOS-27-next-to-MacBook-Pro-Running-macOS-27.jpg?lossy)
For a quick overview of what's new in macOS Golden Gate, be sure to check out our list of 10 features to try first, including Siri AI, easier creation of Shortcuts and Safari Extensions, performance improvements, and more, and then move on to our guide to 50 new features and changes for a more in-depth look.
Apple Says iPhone 18 Pro Max Sold in U.S. Differs in One Way
Following last week's introduction of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, there was some confusion over the cellular modems included in the devices, with it appearing that Apple's own C2 modem was only included in the iPhone 18 Pro.
![Apple iPhone 18 Pro 2up 16x9 1](https://images.macrumors.com/t/IGFWDLa9PJ79ihtmZ0OuIdbI3ew=/400x0/article-new/2026/09/Apple-iPhone-18-Pro-2up-16x9-1.jpg?lossy)
Apple later updated its spec pages for the new models around the world, making it clear that the C2 is included in both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in every country around the world EXCEPT for the iPhone 18 Pro Max in the United States. That device continues to use the Qualcomm Snapdragon X80 modem from the iPhone 17 Pro models, but Apple has yet to explain the reason for this difference.
Reminder: iOS 27's All-New Siri AI Has a Waitlist, Here's How to Sign Up
If you recently installed iOS 27 on your iPhone, you might be wondering where the new-and-improved Siri AI and dedicated Siri app are. In case you missed it, you must join Apple's waitlist in order to gain access to these new features.
![Personalized Siri iOS 27](https://images.macrumors.com/t/uDGySbpuSNItG5nCDRDrMOEJgDs=/400x0/article-new/2026/06/Personalized-Siri-iOS-27.jpg?lossy)
Keep in mind that while iOS 27 is compatible with the iPhone 11 and newer, Siri AI is limited to the iPhone 15 Pro and newer. It is also not currently available at all in EU countries due to Apple's regulatory battle with the European Commission over Digital Markets Act requirements.
For those who are eligible for Siri AI, joining the waitlist is a simple process in the Settings app. Once on the list, wait times seem to vary, with some users receiving access to Siri AI within a few minutes of signing up and others having to wait a few hours or even days.
Apple Releases First iOS 27.2 Beta
With iOS 27.0 out the door, Apple this week seeded the first beta of iOS 27.2 and related updates to developers for testing purposes. Yes, that's right...iOS 27.2, not 27.1.
![iOS 27](https://images.macrumors.com/t/0qk8uvv9xpnnXXjGIVY8PRwLBPg=/400x0/article-new/2026/09/iOS-27.2-Next-to-iPhone.jpg?lossy)
The biggest change in the first iOS 27.2 beta is the revamped Health app that Apple showed off at last week's iPhone event, although Apple says it won't be included in the public release of the update, so the general public will need to wait a bit longer for it to be available. For more, check out our full list of everything new in the first beta of iOS 27.2.
iCloud+ Now Includes Apple TV, Apple Arcade, and Curated Apple Music Stations in Over 100 Countries
Apple this week announced a new subscription initiative that turns paid iCloud+ subscriptions into a broader services bundle in more than 100 countries.
![Apple iCloud Plus expansion hero scaled](https://images.macrumors.com/t/EefpBl7zNggmdd-DHsQtqdyYvqI=/400x0/article-new/2026/09/Apple-iCloud-Plus-expansion-hero-scaled.jpg?lossy)
In select countries, Apple says every paid iCloud+ plan, including the cheapest 50GB tier, now includes Apple TV and Apple Arcade "at no additional cost," while family sharing extends the storage, TV and Arcade access to up to five people.
The initiative does not include the U.S., Canada, Australia, nor is it offered in the UK and other European markets, but it is clearly more than a promotional offer, since Apple TV and Apple Arcade will stop being sold as individual subscriptions through Apple in countries where it has launched.
MacRumors Newsletter
Each week, we publish an email newsletter like this highlighting the top Apple stories, making it a great way to get a bite-sized recap of the week hitting all of the major topics we've covered and tying together related stories for a big-picture view.
So if you want to have top stories like the above recap delivered to your email inbox each week, subscribe to our newsletter!
summary: Apple has released major software updates including iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS Golden Gate, all featuring new Siri AI capabilities. Meanwhile, newly launched hardware includes the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, though the U.S. version of the Pro Max uses a Qualcomm modem instead of Apple's C2 modem. Additionally, Apple expanded paid iCloud+ subscriptions in over 100 countries to include Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no extra cost.
key_points: iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate are now available, featuring new Siri AI capabilities and updates like Visual Intelligence.
Users must sign up for a waitlist to access iOS 27's Siri AI, which is limited to iPhone 15 Pro and newer models and unavailable in EU countries.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max sold in the United States uses a Qualcomm Snapdragon X80 modem rather than Apple's C2 modem found in other regions.
Apple seeded the first iOS 27.2 beta, which features a revamped Health app for developers.
Paid iCloud+ plans in over 100 countries now bundle Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional cost.

title: Laser Your Way Into Debug Mode On The RP2350
author: Tyler August
content:
The RP2350 is actually a pretty secure chip, all things considered. It has secure boot, ARMv8’s TrustZone to split secure and non-secure execution, and you can permanently disable debug — the Pi Foundation even included glitch detection, meaning the traditional ‘zap the chip until it obeys’ technique is blocked. That’s why the [Ledger Donjon] security team went full Bond Villain and strapped everyone’s favourite fruit-flavoured microcontroller to a table with a slowly-approaching laser beam.
![](https://hackaday.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/rp2350-laser-exploit-bench.jpg?w=188)
Okay — movie clichés aside, the laser was in fact very carefully focused on target before they turned it on. That target was the register that enables the 2350’s debug features. Said register was located by decapsulating the chip and examining the die with photon-emission electron microscopy; the actual attack was carried out on a chip that had been decapped on the back side, with IR shining through the silicon wafer. There was probably more than a little trial-and-error to figure out exactly where on the die adjacent to the register to zap with the laser to flip those bits. But flip they did, restoring the debugger’s access to the secure execution zone. Then, after resetting the chip, [Ledger]’s team read the 128-bit secret the Pi Foundation hid in memory as part of the 2350 hacking challenge.
It’s long been accepted that once the black hats — or white hats, for that matter — have their hands on your hardware, they’re going to find a way in. The effort it takes to break into a simple microcontroller here is actually kind of impressive. We’ve talked about laser fault injection before; ironically, we’ve also featured Pi Pico-powered glitching attacks — the kind that this chip’s glitch detection thwarts.
summary: The Ledger Donjon security team successfully bypassed the security features of the RP2350 microcontroller using a focused laser fault injection attack. By decapsulating the chip and targeting the specific register that enables debug features with infrared light, they were able to restore debugger access to the secure execution zone. This allowed them to reset the chip and successfully read a 128-bit secret hidden in memory as part of the Pi Foundation's hacking challenge.
key_points: The RP2350 microcontroller features robust security, including secure boot, TrustZone, permanent debug disable options, and glitch detection.
The Ledger Donjon team used photon-emission electron microscopy on a decapsulated chip to locate the register enabling debug features.
A carefully focused infrared laser was used to flip bits near the target register through the silicon wafer.
The successful laser fault injection attack restored debugger access, enabling the team to read a 128-bit secret hidden in memory.

title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Is Getting A Manga Series, Here's The Key Art
author: Liam Doolan
content:
Original Story: [Thu 6th Aug, 2026 03:15 BST]:
Alongside other Direct news this week, Nintendo has announced Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave will be getting its own manga adaptation.
This announcement was shared on the official Fire Emblem social media account and at the very end of the Japanese Fire Emblem Direct. The first prologue chapter will appear in the October 2026 issue of Shueisha's Saikyo Jump, due out 4th September 2026. It will also be featured in the Shonen Jump+ app.
The manga artist Kazurou Kyou, who was behind the Fire Emblem Engage manga, is also working on this latest series. As noted by Siliconera, the adaptation of Engage (which currently has no official English localisation) has been about for around three years, with the final volume launching in Japan earlier this week.
No details have been shared about what exactly to expect just yet, but we do have the key artwork which features the four heroes, the main protagonist, and various other characters you'll face in the new game.
![Fire Emblem](https://images.nintendolife.com/9717e884c8ef2/fire-emblem.original.jpg) Key art for the Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave manga —
Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave will arrive exclusively for the Switch 2 on 17th September 2026. Here's a bit about the game's story. You can find out more in our previous coverage.
"The Dagdan Empire: a land at the peak of prosperity under the rule of the gods. In the Empire’s capital city of Dagsion, worthy fighters from all over the land arrive to compete in the Heroic Games, with the winner granted one wish. Among the combatants are four Heroes tied to the fate of the world.
"Five years after the Heroic Games, the Dagdan Empire faces its end at the hands of the revived demon god, Balor. Four Heroes who played a significant role in the Heroic Games have vanished. To confront the situation, the progenitor god Sothis charges one soul with saving the world from its end. That soul is you."
summary: Nintendo has announced a manga adaptation for the upcoming game Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, following an announcement at the Japanese Fire Emblem Direct and on social media. The manga is illustrated by Kazurou Kyou and is set to launch its first prologue chapter on September 4, 2026. Meanwhile, the game itself is scheduled for exclusive release on the Switch 2 on September 17, 2026.
key_points: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is receiving a manga adaptation by artist Kazurou Kyou.
The first prologue chapter debuts in Shueisha's Saikyo Jump and Shonen Jump+ on September 4, 2026.
The game is scheduled for an exclusive release on the Switch 2 on September 17, 2026.
The game's plot involves four Heroes competing in the Heroic Games in the Dagdan Empire before facing a revived demon god named Balor.

title: NEW LEAK: Early Look at The Sims Project Rene - Back When It Was Meant to Be The Sims 5
author: Jovan
content:
Turns out that all the years of reporting on The Sims 5 were true after all.
Maxis and Electronic Arts were indeed working on The Sims 5. Or at least that's what Project Rene initially was until it took several turns and expanded into two projects.
Table of Contents
Project Rene WAS The Sims 5
The game's Art Director Mark Holmes, who worked on The Sims Project Rene for almost 6 years referred to the project as "Sims 5". He worked on the game as both a Principle Narrative Designer and Art Director.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-19-at-21.26.31-b01781-1024x196.jpg)
So, what went wrong?
We reported as soon as the development started back in August 2018 that a next generation Sims game is in development. Also referred to as The Sims 5.
The project quickly got an official statement that it was in development by EA CEO Andrew Wilson, who revealed that the next generation Sims game would be both single player and multiplayer. Some additional reportings of The Sims Project Lotus being in development surfaced back in 2021, with exciting patents for new technologies and career opportunities hinting at Story and Narrative Features.
This was all concluded with the final reveal of The Sims Project Rene back in October 2022, when The Sims 4 went free-to-play and excitement came over for a next generation Sims game. Unfortunately, it appeared that The Sims 4 going free-to-play would delay a lot of things. And seemingly cancel them.
The essential team that made The Sims 5 and Project Rene a reality dispersed by 2024. The Art Director that revealed the words of "The Sims 5" above was in development left in October 2023, with Grant Rodiek announcing their departure just 3 months after.
By 2024, it would be confirmed that The Sims 5 is not happening. Instead we got a lot more Sims 4 content and promises of The Sims Project Rene - which in the beginning of this year was referred to as a Mobile-first multiplayer experience.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/G-PJWWBWgAA5cjT.jpeg)
The latest Sims insider talks revolve around The Sims Project X, which is a mix of The Sims 4 and The Sims Project Rene technology. The game supposedly has a deadline until September next year, and the focus on it is bigger than on Project Rene (Multiplayer) - which EA has allegedly already completed for launch.
The Sims Project Rene as The Sims 5 Development: Early Concepts and Research & Development
We found the following images on Twitter / X thanks to user @PattonKieran, who shared early images of The Sims Project Rene when it was being developed as The Sims 5.
Keep in mind that The Sims 5 / The Sims Project Rene was always meant to be a multi-platform experience from the start. the only split that happened later was making The Sims Project Rene a multiplayer-only experience, with The Sims Project X taking the place now as a single-player only experience.
The following images and material were shared by multiple developers online, later reposted on Twitter. Note that they don't represent the final state of what the games could look like - only early research, exploration and game and concept development. The Sims Project Lotus seems to be the early stage name of The Sims Project Rene, also carrying the new simulation technology of Dynamic Motives which technically were in a shape of a lotus. This would later be carried over into the current version of Rene and possibly The Sims Project X.
The Sims Project Lotus
The following images and work shown below was done and published by developer Geoffrey C Mitchell.
![CONVERSATION 2](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/CONVERSATION-2-1024x758.png)
According to the portfolio, the team was exploring:
- Mobile play + cross-platform synergy
- Synchronous, asynchronous & asymmetric multiplayer
- Story-driven gameplay with narrative customization and sharing
- More unique, authentic and dynamic Sims and relationships
Established interactive Simulation Gameplay platform and modular implementation dev tool-set to fundamental re-imagine a Sims experience that is:
Mobile play and cross-platform synergy - Multiplayer, synchronous, async., and asymmetric Story-driven with narrative customization & sharing Empowered by better, more unique, authentic, dynamic characters & connections
One of the most interesting concepts was Dynamic Motives. The idea was to give Sims motivations based not only on basic needs, but also on their character and current condition, making their behavior feel more meaningful and authentic.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-19-at-21.52.51-26ec96-1024x441.jpg)
Maxis was also experimenting with different layers of simulation time: Generation → Year → Week → Day → Time of Day → Routine → Activity → Action. These layers could support things like family trees, world story progression, calendars, work schedules, daily routines and day/night cycles.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-19-at-22.01.23-a85512-493x1024.jpg)
There’s also a “Morning Routine” prototype showing how Sims could follow context-based behavior: wake up → check needs → shower/use the bathroom → get ready → eat
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-19-at-22.00.51-332110-1024x458.jpg)
The Sims Project Rene - Early Development Screens
The following screens shared publicly by Mark Cordell represent early work on The Sims Project Rene from 2018 to 2023:
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-2-b1a7f3-1024x454.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-3-b226bf-1024x454.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-4-39a554-1024x454.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-5-b2e2a5-1024x454.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-6-f82448-1024x454.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-7-b390d8-1024x454.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-8-dc4cde-1024x454.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-9-0e49c0-1024x454.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/the-sims-5-the-sims-project-rene-early-dev-screens-1-836f75-1024x454.jpg)
The images above represent various explorations for The Sims Project Rene. From lot selection across multiple platforms to how characters react to different environments and objects. Down to how different clothing options can react with physics and animations.
The early exploration phases of The Sims Project Rene also show a much larger map of a Sims-inspired Paris world. With prototypes showing much larger streets, more crowded neighborhoods and more.
Each clothing piece seems to have a concept for different modular endings and variations, with furniture being designed with new Sim characters in mind to match different animation scenarios.
The Sims Project Rene, when it was meant to be The Sims 5, looked like an ambitious and very large project. But do keep in mind that The Sims 4 was also like that at start. One of the developers shared Titanopolis - an early pre-production world that never saw the light of day. The big beautiful SimParisian landscapes have been reduced to small multiplayer corner gatherings from what we could see in recent playtests.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/the-sims-project-rene-city-life-game-with-friends-playtest-screen-preview-24.jpg)
Hopefully some of the bigger HD technology showcased above is being used for the upcoming Project X release.
What are your thoughts on The Sims Project Rene from the days when it was meant to be The Sims 5? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below and stay tuned for more Sims News on Sims Community!
summary: Maxis and Electronic Arts initially developed Project Rene—formerly known as Project Lotus—to serve as the next-generation Sims 5 before the project expanded, split, and faced team departures by 2024. Leaked early concepts and developer portfolios revealed that the game was originally envisioned as an ambitious multi-platform experience featuring cross-platform synergy, story-driven multiplayer, and advanced mechanics like Dynamic Motives. While a traditional Sims 5 is no longer happening, development has shifted toward a mobile-first multiplayer Project Rene and a single-player Project X.
key_points: Project Rene and Project Lotus were early working titles and concepts for what was originally meant to be The Sims 5.
Early development explorations featured cross-platform play, various multiplayer modes, narrative customization, and larger maps like a Sim-inspired Paris world.
Developers experimented with advanced simulation mechanics such as Dynamic Motives and multi-layered simulation time ranging from generations down to daily routines.
Key team members departed by 2024, leading to the cancellation of the traditional Sims 5 plan in favor of a mobile-first multiplayer Project Rene and the single-player Project X.

title: Apple Explains Why the iPhone 18 Pro Has a Variable Aperture
author: Jeremy Gray
content:
The Apple iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have arrived, and their familiar outward appearance belies a major change to the main camera. For the first time, an iPhone features a variable aperture, and PetaPixel spoke with Apple to learn firsthand why it was created, how it works, and what it means for how people capture photos and videos on Apple’s latest flagship phone.
This was a rare chance to have a candid, unscripted conversation with Apple and gain valuable insight into how the company approaches the engineering and design decisions of one of its most important and valuable product lines, the iPhone Pro.
Why Is Now the Right Time for a Variable Aperture on iPhone?
Perhaps the most pressing question about the iPhone 18 Pro series’ new variable-aperture main camera is, “Why now?” Apple has had plenty of opportunities to introduce a variable aperture before, and many of its competitors have done just that.
“Especially on our Pro line, we really want to make it as simple as possible for anyone to get the best shot possible, all while giving really technically advanced capabilities for pros, people who may be experienced in photography and videography,” says Jeremy Hendricks of Apple’s iPhone Product Marketing team.
“Our Pro line over the years has really had to evolve and balance both of those sides,” Hendricks continues.
As it happens, it was less about why introduce the variable aperture now, and much more about how to improve image quality. The new variable aperture was, at least at first, a means to an end.
“So we really started from sensitivity, actually. We’re always trying to make our cameras better, bring better image quality to customers,” Matt Waldon, Senior Director of Camera & Depth Hardware at Apple, tells PetaPixel. “And in this case, we really wanted to improve the sensitivity. And there’s a few ways to do that.”
![A curved, modern building with floor-to-ceiling glass walls and illuminated horizontal light strips overlooks a grassy embankment at night.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/IMG_0004-converted-DNG-800x600.jpg)
As Waldon explains, you can increase the image sensor size; that’s a surefire way to improve sensitivity, all else equal. However, this has drawbacks. Bigger sensors require more physical space, bigger lenses, and more processing power, for starters.
For Apple, the better solution was to make a faster aperture. In the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s case, that meant going from an f/1.8 aperture to an f/1.48 one.
![A close-up view of the back of a deep red smartphone, showing a raised camera module with three circular lenses, a flash, and a small sensor against a soft pink background.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/iphone-aperture-story-4-800x420.jpg)
“So this camera now has an f/1.48 lens,” Waldon says. “And if we did that without variable aperture, in some shots, for example, if you’re shooting somebody close and you have something in the background you want to capture… you would really lose sharpness and not necessarily be able to take the shot you want to take.”
Variable aperture then became a necessary engineering challenge to overcome because Apple wanted to increase the speed of the iPhone’s lens without worsening image quality when a faster aperture isn’t needed.
![A composite image showing four vertical strips of a brick wall, each labeled with a ranking and an aperture setting: f/1.4.8, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/iPhone-18-Pro-Sharpness-800x450.jpg)
Giving Photographers More Creative Control
As Hendricks says, though, variable aperture offers many benefits to the end user beyond better photo and video quality. It also gives serious photographers and videographers more creative control over how their content looks, and that’s right up Apple’s alley.
“So when you look at something like aperture, that seemed like the next natural thing to bring to the Pro camera system, [to] be able to expand that overall creative range for everyone,” Hendricks explains.
Waldon remarks that Apple got really excited about the creative possibilities the variable aperture system offers.
“Being able to shorten the depth of field even beyond what you can shoot with today at f/1.8. Being able to close down the aperture gives you more things you can do when it comes to video. You can have more flexibility in shutter speed. Even in stills, you can have more flexibility in shutter speed. When you want it, you can get this very cool starburst effect,” Waldon says.
Six Aperture Blades Struck the Right Balance
Speaking of that starburst effect, the stepless variable aperture mechanism incorporates six precisely designed, equally rigorously engineered blades. Why six?
“So six blades was really a combination of things. One is just the physical dimensions of it. The more blades you add, given the size constraints, it becomes difficult to fit them all in, frankly. So there’s, there’s a physical constraint,” Waldon tells PetaPixel.
![A close-up view of a mechanical camera aperture mechanism with overlapping black blades centered within a circular housing.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/iphone-aperture-story-1-800x420.jpg)
“Obviously we want enough blades to give sort of a nice, smooth aperture at every setting. So we did a lot of optimization around the shape of the blades and at every aperture setting,” he continues. “You sort of see how the blades have a big impact on how bokeh and out of focus areas look. It impacts how the starburst looks. So for this particular design, six was really the sweet spot.”
Each of the six laser-cut aperture blades is constructed from a specialized polymer composite Apple designed to strike the right balance between mass, flexibility, and durability. Each blade is thinner than a human hair and works alongside a new compact rotor mechanism.
“So it’s amazing that you have this incredibly complex camera module, let alone with the rotor mechanism, with all of these different things that enable variable aperture in a really smart way on something that you have just in your pocket all the time with you,” Hendricks says.
![Bright sun shines in a clear blue sky above a forest of tall, dark evergreen trees.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/IMG_0577-600x800.jpg)
Of course, in typical Apple fashion, each aspect of the new variable aperture is described with hype-generating language. Still, there’s no question that no detail is too small when it comes to the iPhone 18 Pro’s key new camera feature. Every millimeter of space inside the phone is precious, and conflicting goals often come into play. Fitting a stepless variable aperture system into a relatively small smartphone camera module is no easy feat, as evidenced by the fact that many companies that have done it before ultimately stopped doing it in subsequent models.
Each Aperture Value Has Its Place
As for the stepless design, the users themselves, at least for now, only have access to four aperture settings. Mobile photographers and videographers can switch between f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4, though the default is f/1.8.
Apple says f/1.8 remains the best overall choice because it is very sharp, still delivers some background blur when the subject is close to the camera (as it often is), and is familiar to users. It strikes a good balance between sharpness and speed.
![A person with curly hair wearing a red blouse and tan pants stands in a field of tall, dry grass in front of a long, modern building under a blue sky with scattered clouds.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/IMG_0045-converted-DNG-800x600.jpg)
“So there is a little bit of trade off as you go to to higher or lower apertures, where you sacrifice a little bit of sharpness [at f/1.48 because of aberrations] and on the long end, [f/4], because of diffraction,” Waldon explains.
Even if f/1.8, or at least near it, is the optimal aperture in many situations, Apple is committed to giving users more choice. Hendricks and Waldon are especially interested in how videographers use the variable aperture to dial in the perfect shutter speed for the look they want.
![A black and white landscape view of the sheer granite face of Half Dome rising above a forested mountain ridge.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/IMG_0609-stark-black-and-white-800x600.jpg)
Pro Controls
For Apple, the variable aperture plus the new Pro Controls on iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are a perfect pairing for creativity. Until now, iPhone owners had to use a third-party app to get granular camera control. While those third-party apps still offer a lot and may remain the right choice for some, Apple believes that Pro Controls will both introduce more people to manual camera controls as a general concept and also satisfy more serious users like us, who have been asking for advanced controls inside Apple’s Camera app for years.
“[Pro Controls] kind of invite people to learn about manual controls and try to experiment with them, even if you don’t have a deep background in that,” Hendricks says.
“The incredible thing with the Camera app and Pro controls is everything is by default automatic. So you don’t have to know how to use a camera. Just as has always been the case, you just go in, press the shutter button, let the camera do the work,” Waldon adds.
“But at the same time, once you start playing around with it, I think it’s actually really fun and almost a little bit hard to put down when you start playing around with all the different settings,” he continues.
“The amazing thing now is that now that you do have the full control, you take advantage of the computational image pipeline. So you get the image quality, you get the Styles, you also get on the video side, that flexibility that we have with editing, like audio mix, for example,” Hendricks adds.
“The more flexibility that you give people upfront, like in our Camera app, the more creative range that they’ll have,” he says.
A Cascading Series of Events That Changed the iPhone 18 Pro’s Camera System
Apple is far from the first company to experiment with a variable aperture in its smartphone camera system. However, Apple is exhibiting a distinct amount of care in its approach.
“We went into this very intentionally,” Waldon says. “You’ll see that it does make a real difference when you’re shooting in scenes, when you have something close and you have something far and you want more depth of field. It’s a real thing.”
Waldon says he’s aware of how Apple’s competitors have implemented variable apertures before, and he thinks that in many cases, “the difference isn’t really there.”
“For [our] optical format and f-number, this is the right time to maintain fantastic quality and also give this creativity.”
![Pedestrians wait at a street corner in a city while a man with a backpack and headphones walks across the foreground.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/IMG_0511-stack-black-and-white-800x600.jpg)
Unlike some other companies that quickly abandoned variable apertures for a variety of reasons, Waldon says Apple is all in on the design decision.
“We think this is something that is super important for our Pro cameras and it’s part of our plan going forward.”
It’s interesting to consider that everything that has changed about the iPhone 18 Pro camera system ultimately started from a single, relatively simple desire: Improving image quality in low light.
There were multiple ways to achieve this goal, and Apple ultimately settled on a faster aperture. But you don’t always want a fast aperture, so it needed to be variable. And if the phone has a variable aperture, then the user should be able to control it, right? Enter Pro controls.
Each of these changes taken individually may not seem like a big deal, and arguably we weren’t totally convinced out of the gate that much had truly changed with the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera system. However, in real-world use, all of these tweaks add up to a significantly better camera experience for both photography and video.
Image creditsApple. iPhone 18 Pro product photos by Erin Thomson for PetaPixel. Real-world samples by Jaron Schneider.
summary: The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max introduce a new variable-aperture main camera system developed primarily to improve sensitivity and image quality. Apple engineered a stepless system featuring six specialized polymer blades to support creative control for both novice and advanced users. Users can manually select settings between f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4, with f/1.8 serving as the default balance between sharpness and speed.
key_points: The iPhone 18 Pro introduces Apple's first variable-aperture main camera, moving from an f/1.8 aperture to a faster f/1.48 option.
Apple selected a six-blade stepless design utilizing a specialized polymer composite to balance physical size constraints, durability, and bokeh quality.
Users can manually adjust between four aperture settings (f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4), while f/1.8 remains the default choice.
The new variable aperture hardware pairs with native Pro Controls inside Apple's Camera app to offer expanded manual control and creative range for photography and videography.

title: Preparing For The Next Sims 4 Update (Tutorial & Countdown)
author: Nooboofever
content:
The Next Sims 4 Update is Landing on September 22nd, 2026! Be safe, not sorry!
With over 95+ bug fixes and multiple corrections to simulation lag and other errors, this next major Sims 4 Update is going to be a large one. As with any major update, you need to make preparations if you want to make sure your existing game files will be safe, by backing them up and taking proper precautions. Read on for some guided assistance, general tips, and what to expect when the next Sims 4 Update drops September 22nd!
Table of Contents
What is Coming with The Sims 4 September Patch?
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/laundrylist2-1024x576.jpg)
As this patch is one of many Sims 4 Updates that have come out in the last year, focusing less on new content and more on bug fixes, the list is fairly heavy. The recent Laundry List from September 15th addresses many questions, and lists the fixes expected to arrive next Tuesday!
TLDR of the Sims 4 September Update Laundry List
- Improved Autonomy: Focus on improving Sims' autonomous behavior, including Sims maintaining eye contact during chats, using bathroom sinks instead of kitchen sinks, and low-energy Sims no longer waking up to do random tasks.
- Bug Fixes & Stability: 95+ bug fixes including 10 significant crash and stability improvements, top community issues from the EA Forums like Married Sims reverting to partners, and Sims getting stuck in interaction queues.
- Relationship Balancing: Tuning to Lovestruck (slower romantic decay, no satisfaction changes for inactive households) and Growing Together (improving dynamic frequency and making low-compatibility Sims realistically avoid one another).
- Looking Ahead: Our October Base Game update will shift its focus toward Food, Dining, and Drink improvements.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/the-sims-4-free-content-drops-teaser6-1024x576.jpg)
There's also the question of what additional content may arrive with this update; After the free content teaser drop back in August that showcased new clothes, hairs, and build/buy mode items, players have been waiting to see the rest of the content to arrive later this year.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/the-sims-4-free-content-drops-teaser11-1024x576.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/TS4Patch-SD-J3-66e481-1024x576.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/TS4Patch-NewSim03-5-351fcf-1024x576.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/TS4Patch-NewSim04-2-234dad-1024x576.jpg)
The first drop included an expansion on clothing intended to flatter plus-sized Sims or be more size inclusive, as well as a sculpted afro-textured star-themed hairstyle.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/the-sims-4-free-content-drops-teaser13-1024x576.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/the-sims-4-free-content-drops-teaser7-1024x576.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/the-sims-4-free-content-drops-teaser3-1024x576.jpg)
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/the-sims-4-free-content-drops-teaser8-1024x576.jpg)
Remaining items we could see released include multiple additional new hairstyles, tons of new CAS content for children, as well as a wide variety of kitschy and stylistically varied build and buy mode items, including a new fish tank, clutter items, bedroom furniture, etc.
Saving your Save Files!
Especially if you are a Mods & Custom Content user and/or you play long-term save files like legacies, challenges, forever saves, etc., an important part of save file health and keeping them safe and playable is to back them up prior to updates.
This is primarily important for those who play with mods and custom content, as mods being disabled after previously being active in a save or mods being broken while active in a save can cause corruption and other issues.
Although creating back ups of files can sound a bit daunting if you're unfamiliar with the concept, it is fairly easy and painless.
Here are the steps for backing up saves:
- Go to your save files folder. This will vary depending on your operating system.
  - For Windows PC: C:\Users\[USERNAME]\Documents\Electronic Arts\The Sims 4\saves
  - For MacOS: Macintosh HD/Users/User/Documents/Electronic Arts/The Sims 4/saves
![sims 4 update september](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-85.png)
- Copy any save files you want to back up for safe keeping. These will just be numbers so finding them may be slightly difficult, but anything recently played will automatically be at the top. You can also choose to sort files by the date they were last edited, and anything recently saved over should be at the top.
  - If you’re not sure, a good practice is to just copy all your saves to a backup folder.
  - This can also be done with Your Sims 4 tray files, which are the files that contain the data for anything saved in your library through the Sims 4 Gallery.
    - For Windows PC: C:\Users\[USERNAME]\Documents\Electronic Arts\The Sims 4\tray
    - For MacOS: Macintosh HD/Users/User/Documents/Electronic Arts/The Sims 4/tray
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/paste.jpg)
- To back up your files, save them to separate locations. These can be folders on your computer (Like on your desktop or in a separate section of your documents folder), but it is recommended to use separate storage in case of hardware issues. These can include a USB flash drive, external hard drive, a cloud program, etc.
  - A good tip is to place them in a folder with the date of the back ups as the folder name.
- If a save needs to be restored to a previous version, you can just copy paste from the folder back into your main Sims 4 Saves folder directly.
Another good rule of thumb is that, if playing with mods or custom content, do not attempt to play save files you care about until creators have posted about the update and the status of their mods. Most major creators post fairly quickly, but be patient!
Mods Folders & The 50/50 Method
The Sims Team confirmed in a message on The Sims Discord that this Sims 4 Update will have an impact on mods:
This update is expected to have an impact on mods and we recommend you back up your saves and manage your mods/CC carefully.
Like most other updates, mods have a chance of breaking, especially if they change a feature that has been adjusted in the update. Custom content is often completely fine, but files can always corrupt or go wrong in some way. This means that, while it may seem tedious, the 50/50 method is the best way to find any issues that have popped up in your game that are stemming from broken or corrupted mods and custom content.
The 50/50 method is a way of organizing and testing mods and custom content to track down a specific file or files that are causing a bug or error in your game, or are causing it to not load or crash. Make sure to back up your saves, mods, and tray folders prior to this!
For a more in-depth guide to the 50/50 method, ThatSimsLady has broken it down previously and provided a guide that walks you through it, but here’s a general diagram from Sims After Dark.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-86-1024x588.png)
Basically, the 50/50 method is when you split your mods folder down the middle, testing each half (Say, Half A and Half B) individually to rule out issues. For example, if the error or bug in questions persists in Half A but not Half B, then you know that the issue is held in Half A. You can safely sort away Half B and then split Half A and test either half, and so on and so forth.
This should help you track down problematic files fairly easily. And I will say that nobody likes doing the 50/50 method since it can take a long time, especially if you play with loads of mods and custom content, but is a very good way to make sure your game is in healthy condition and none of your saves are at risk.
In most cases, mods that break during updates are UI Mods and Gameplay Mods.
Gameplay Mods generally add or change features in The Sims 4, and many contain two files; .package and .ts4script files. While not always, these mods are prone to breaking with updates and should be removed and separately tested, or only updated/added back in once the creator has said it is safe.
UI Mods are any mods that change the user interface, like the menus surrounding your screen in Live mode and Build mode, or your columns in Create-A-Sim. The most commonly used UI mods include UI Cheats, More Columns in CAS, and any User Interface Replacement mods. While it is not inherent that they will break, they are usually the first to break during any update.
Also, always delete your thumbcache file. It regenerates every time the game launches, and should always be deleted while changing your mods folder in any way, especially if you're doing the 50/50 method.
It is also recommended to test mods with new updates in a completely fresh save file, to avoid corruption but also since certain updates only work with newer saves.
Other Points of Note for Mod Organization & The 50/50 Method
- A good rule of thumb is to keep all mods separate from custom content. Custom content can break, but it is very unlikely since they often don't change anything about the games functions or features, and instead just add new assets.
  - You cannot separate mods from their extra files. If you have two files for a mod, like "MODNAME.package" and "MODNAME.ts4script", those two files must always be in the same folder to function.
- Mod dependencies are larger mods that don't do much on their own, but are required for others to function. Many smaller mods require things like Lot51's Core File, the XML injector, Lumpinou's Mood Pack, and many others that must be tested alongside mods that require them.
  - These may also need to be updated on their own.
- Some easy ways to organize your custom content and mods include...
  - NOTE: Script mods can only be one folder deep, while custom content can go around five folders deep.
  - By Type: You can organize by the type of asset, area of the game, etc., and it really just depends on how detailed you want to go.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-2.png)
- Ex: Placing hairs in a folder called "Hairs", "CAS_Hairs", "CAS", or even more detailed folders like "Hairs_Infant_Fem" or any variant.
- You can also make an overall "Create-A-Sim" folder, and then add individual folders for things like hair, makeup, etc.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-1.png)
- By Creator: While this can get semi-tricky when creators have collaborations, it can be easier to avoid duplicate mod files by sorting by creator, especially if you have lots of items from a select few.
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-3.png)
- Ex: "Creator1", "Creator2", "Creator3".
![](https://simscommunity.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-4.png)
- If you only have a handful of items from a certain creator, you can also alphabetically sort. Like "A-D", and include all creators with names starting with that range of letters.
The biggest point is that your organization method makes sense to you, and you alone! As long as you can find where you put things and troubleshoot your
Countdown to The Sims 4 September Patch Release
The upcoming Sims 4 September Patch is set to release on September 22nd, 2026 at 10AM PT / 7PM CET / 6PM BT across PC, Mac, Xbox and Playstation supported platforms. To make things easier we’ve included a handy countdown below that’ll tell exactly when the latest Patch is available to download.
What do you think is coming next from the free content release? Let us know, and follow Sims Community for all your news about The Sims and other Life Simulation games!
summary: The major Sims 4 update is scheduled to launch on September 22, 2026, bringing over 95 bug fixes, stability improvements, and autonomy adjustments. Because the patch is expected to affect mods and custom content, players are strongly advised to back up their save files and tray folders beforehand. Additionally, the article outlines troubleshooting strategies like the 50/50 method to help users identify broken or corrupted mods after the update.
key_points: The upcoming Sims 4 update arrives on September 22, 2026, across PC, Mac, Xbox, and PlayStation.
The patch features over 95 bug fixes, relationship balancing, and improvements to autonomous behavior.
Players should back up their save and tray files to separate storage locations before applying the update to prevent file corruption.
The 50/50 method is recommended for tracking down broken gameplay or UI mods after the patch is installed.
The October Base Game update will focus on improvements to food, dining, and drinks.

title: Games Workshop: New TonePro Paints, Blood Bowl Goblins, Tomb Kings, and More On The Way
author: Simon Berman
content:
Games Workshop: New TonePro Paints, Blood Bowl Goblins, Tomb Kings, and More On The Way
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/gw-big-uatumn-preview-misc-header.jpg) 
Warhammer’s specialist games and hobby supplies are also getting some reveals in today’s big autumn preview.
The Fall Preview had at least a little bit for almost everyone today. Wrapping things up saw a major facelift for the Tomb Kings of Warhammer: The Old World, an expansion for Warhammer Quest: Darkwater, an all-new Blood Bowl team, and maybe most excitingly of all, a massive expansion to the Warhammer hobby paints line.
Tomb Kings
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/tow-tomb-kings-photo.jpg)
A new box set for Tomb Kings armies reveals no new units, but a ton of new sculpts! When Tomb Kings returned to The Old World, they did so with some suitably ancient models. But this new box will be the first time you can get your hands on a refresh of the army’s most important models.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/tow-tombs1.jpg)
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/tow-tombs2.jpg)
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/tow-tombs3.jpg)
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image4-05-imr6frxikr.jpg) 
The core skeleton units of the Tomb Kings army hadn’t been updated in decades, and frankly, they were showing their age. This new set of models includes updated sculpts and kits for the three core units of hosts of Settra. Their release will also be accompanied by a supplement, Arcane Journal: River of Bones.
Blood Bowl – Night Goblins
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/blood-bowl-new-gobbos.jpg)
For the first time, Blood Bowl coaches will be able to field teams entirely composed of Night Goblins and their questionably tamed squigs. Forgoing the secret weapons of standard goblins, Night Goblins focus on their fungal friends to win the day. Four new positionals make up this team’s elite: Cave Squigs. Squig Wranglers. Squig Hoppers, and Squig Herders. The box includes two of each plus six Night Goblin Linemen. Rules for this team will be first released in the upcoming 23rd issue of Spike! Journal.
Warhammer Quest Darkwater: Agents of the Order of Azyr
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/warhammer-quest-agents.jpg) 
The first expansion for Warhammer Quest’s latest incarnation is just over the horizon. The Agents of the Order of Azyr are four new heroes who are here to cleanse the Jade Abbey of Nurgle’s foul touch. The band is led by witch hunter Safiya Ashcross, who is followed by the sharpshooter Caul Durnan, drawn from the Wildercorps, Brother Belias, a devout priest of the Great Wheel, and the Bright Wizard Ignus Sharn. The set is accompanied by all the cards necessary to use these heroes in your games of Warhammer Quest: Darkwater.
Warhammer TonePro
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/warhammer-protone1.jpg)
Finally, today sees a huge update to the venerable (formerly known as Citadel) Warhammer paint line. TonePro is a range of 150 new paints and promises to offer deeply saturated hues from paints with strong opacity, requiring fewer coats to achieve solid coverage.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/warhammer-protone2.png) 
The paints are designed around stepped sets of five hues starting with bases and moving up to extreme highlights. A pair of new mediums accompany the set, including a Shading Medium that essentially allows you to make a shade with the properties of a shade like Nuln Oil or Agrax Earthshade from any paint in the range. As well, a blending medium with different opacity will also be included. The Foundation paints themselves promise carefully designed flow properties that leave consistent coverage even when drybrushed.
Unsurprisingly, this leads into a smaller reveal for a new set of Warhammer-branded “makeup” style dry brushes that have become a community favorite over the past decade.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/brushes-01-migrh2tcgz.jpg)
The range will be demoed at Warhammer stores and your FLGS starting next Saturday, 09/26/26.
Do I own enough paints? Probably. Will I buy too many new ones? Almost certainly.
![Simon Berman](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/avatar-simon-berman-300x300-1-150x150.jpg)
summary: Games Workshop announced several major reveals during its autumn preview, including a model refresh for the Tomb Kings in Warhammer: The Old World and a new Night Goblins team for Blood Bowl. The company also unveiled an expansion for Warhammer Quest: Darkwater called Agents of the Order of Azyr. Additionally, Games Workshop introduced Warhammer TonePro, a massive new line of 150 paints, mediums, and specialized dry brushes.
key_points: A new Tomb Kings box set for Warhammer: The Old World introduces updated sculpts for core skeleton units alongside the Arcane Journal: River of Bones supplement.
A new Blood Bowl team features entirely Night Goblins and squigs, with rules debuting in the 23rd issue of Spike! Journal.
The Warhammer Quest: Darkwater expansion, Agents of the Order of Azyr, adds four new heroes and necessary cards to the game.
The Warhammer TonePro paint line includes 150 new highly opaque hues, stepped sets for highlighting, new mediums, and makeup-style dry brushes.

title: AI helps recycle old milk bottles into new plastic packaging
author: Claudia Robinson
content:
![A man wearing safety glasses, an orange fluorescent jacket and white hard hat is standing in front of a huge stack of used plastic cartons](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/51ee/live/ce2968f0-b2ae-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.jpg)
The Biffa Polymers plant uses AI to free up workers for less tedious tasks, managing director James McLeary said
- Published
Artificial intelligence is being used to help turn old milk bottles into new ones and they can be back in your fridge "within two weeks".
Recycling site Biffa Polymers in Redcar uses the technology to analyse materials moving along conveyor belts at a speed and scale that "would be difficult for people to match".
Managing director James McLeary, said AI could identify different types of plastic using optical and infra-red scanning, as well as image analysis.
But he said the plant still relied on a workforce of about 200 people who are freed up by AI to ensure products are of the right quality, rather than "spending their time doing tedious tasks".
![A close-up shot of a bale of flattened, used plastic bottles, some still with their labels on, waiting to be processed at the Redcar recycling plant](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/fa0c/live/aefa9f30-b2ae-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.jpg)
The plant has recycled more than 10 billion plastic bottles in the last 20 years
The technology can analyse images of waste and identify a material's composition.
McLeary said that was "particularly useful" when bottles have been crushed or distorted and they were trying to select high-density polyethylene (HDPE) bottles, which can be recycled for food-grade packaging.
"A milk bottle might be easy to recognise when it is intact, but once crushed its shape can change completely.
"AI systems can be trained to recognise that the different shapes are still milk bottles," he said.
![A close-up of thousands of tiny white plastic pellets, around the size of lentils](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/4ad6/live/e6c67820-b2b4-11f1-a430-4d16ee157c41.jpg)
The tiny HDPE pellets are sent to other factories to be made into new recycled packaging
The Redcar plant - which has now processed the equivalent of more than 10 billion plastic milk bottles in almost 20 years - takes plastic which has already been sorted by type and colour and carries out the final stages of processing.
Material is shredded, washed and separated before being treated and turned into fine plastic pellets.
Those pellets can then be used to produce new packaging, including food-grade material for milk bottles.
![A factory production line covered with flattened old plastic milk bottles passing under an orange light](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/8de7/live/65d83950-b2b5-11f1-a430-4d16ee157c41.jpg)
AI is used for quality control, analysing the plastic bottles to ensure only the right ones are selected for recycling
The company said it was investigating in other robotic systems which could use AI to physically pick out those bottles.
It also uses AI for safety around the site, monitoring cameras and identifying "potential risks... for example, when someone appears to be moving into an area where a vehicle could be operating".
But McLeary said the plant remained reliant on its workforce despite the growing role of technology and that they still need people who are "prepared to do good, hard labour on the lines, sorting stuff very responsibly".
He added that the technology was allowing the recycling process to speed up.
"[A] bottle that you threw away two weeks ago may be back in somebody else's fridge, because that's how quickly the material gets recycled in the UK," McLeary said.
Follow BBC Tees on X,, external Facebook, external, Nextdoor and Instagram, external.
summary: The Biffa Polymers recycling plant in Redcar uses artificial intelligence to quickly analyze materials on conveyor belts, turning old milk bottles into new food-grade packaging within two weeks. The technology utilizes optical and infra-red scanning alongside image analysis to identify crushed or distorted plastic bottles that are difficult for humans to spot manually. While AI increases processing speed and monitors site safety, the plant still relies on its workforce of approximately 200 people to ensure product quality and perform manual sorting.
key_points: Biffa Polymers in Redcar uses AI to analyze plastic materials moving along conveyor belts at high speeds.
The technology identifies crushed or distorted high-density polyethylene (HDPE) milk bottles that are suitable for food-grade packaging.
Recycled plastic is shredded, washed, and turned into tiny pellets, allowing a discarded bottle to return to a fridge as new packaging within two weeks.
AI is also used for site safety by monitoring cameras to detect potential risks involving vehicles and workers.
The recycling plant still employs about 200 workers who focus on product quality and manual labor alongside the technology.

title: Cleveland ex-offender says no punishment would have stopped her
author: Naj Modak; Gary Philipson
content:
![Selfie of a Jade Smith seated on a train, wearing a dark baseball cap and a light grey zip-up fleece jacket with a Berghaus logo. She has facial piercings and short hair visible beneath the cap. Blue-patterned train seats and wood-effect wall panels are visible in the background.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1056/cpsprodpb/f172/live/5bdb0750-b1f9-11f1-be69-3bcaf4441a59.jpg)
Smith said drug use overtook her life and was the driving force behind her offending
- Published
A former offender has said no punishment would have stopped her shoplifting while she was addicted to drugs.
Jade Smith, 35, from Skelton in Cleveland, said she spent all of her money on cocaine and then stole food and household essentials because she had "nothing to live on" until she got paid again.
After convictions, homelessness and a period living in a tent, she is now five to six weeks clean at a rehabilitation facility in Preston and trying to rebuild relationships with her children and family.
Smith said: "I do now think about the shop workers and how they felt. I'd like to apologise. I wish I'd thought at the time how other people would be feeling and not just myself. It was quite selfish really."
Smith said drug use overtook her life and was the driving force behind her offending.
She said she began taking drugs as a teenager and believed the older people she mixed with at the time influenced the path her life took.
Skelton woman "ashamed" of shoplifting past
Although she sometimes used shoplifting to support her addiction, Smith said she often stole everyday essentials after spending her money on cocaine.
"I'd spend all my money on my drugs and then I'd have nothing to live on until I got paid next," she said.
Smith said the fear of being caught was never enough to break the cycle she found herself trapped in.
"When you've got no choice and you think, 'How am I going to live for the month?', you don't really think at the time. You're just thinking of what you need to do."
Asked whether she would have carried on offending despite tougher penalties, she said: "Probably, yeah, because it's just what you've got to do at the time to get through in your life."
Smith said she felt "ashamed", "embarrassed" and guilty about her actions and regretted failing to consider the effect they may have had on shop workers.
'Something needs to change'
She said she was convicted of fraud aged 16 after stealing cheques from her father's cheque book and later sentenced to three years in prison following a street robbery in 2019.
Smith said the consequences of her addiction stretched beyond the criminal justice system and affected those closest to her.
After a period of homelessness, including living in a tent, Smith accepted a place at a rehabilitation facility with support from friends and a charity.
She said being separated from her children was what finally made her realise "something needs to change".
"I do want to put things right, prove to them that I can change and change for good this time and I'm not just saying it," she said.
Shoplifting offences in the Cleveland Police area increased by nearly 15% in the last financial year - the biggest percentage increase in the country.
Cleveland Police said it was committed to tackling the issue and will continue to use all of the tools at their disposal.
Follow BBC Tees on X,, external Facebook, external, Nextdoor and Instagram, external and listen to Radio Tees on BBC Sounds.
summary: Jade Smith, a former offender from Cleveland, stated that no punishment could have stopped her shoplifting while she was struggling with a severe cocaine addiction. After experiencing homelessness, convictions, and time in prison, she is currently in a rehabilitation facility and working to rebuild relationships with her children. Shoplifting offences in the Cleveland Police area increased by nearly 15% in the last financial year, marking the highest percentage increase in the country.
key_points: Jade Smith spent her money on cocaine and stole food and household essentials to survive between paydays.
She stated that the fear of being caught or facing tougher penalties would not have stopped her offending during her addiction.
Smith is now five to six weeks clean at a rehabilitation facility in Preston and hopes to rebuild relationships with her children.
Shoplifting offences in the Cleveland Police area rose by nearly 15% in the last financial year.

title: Sensitive UK police data vulnerable to ‘compromise’ by US government and foreign actors
author: Aisha Down
content:
Vast troves of highly sensitive police data are lying on Microsoft cloud platforms which an oﬃcial UK security assessment deemed to be vulnerable to “compromise” by foreign actors and the US government, a Guardian investigation can reveal.
The files include criminal records, victim statements, internal emails and sensitive information held by more than 40 police forces across the UK.
Some files exceed “oﬃcial” classification, according to a police document seen by the Guardian, raising the possibility the information could be classed as “secret” or “top secret”.
The cloud platform is Microsoft Azure, one of the main commercial offerings of the US tech company. It is used by businesses and governments globally and rests on a web of IT infrastructure – datacentres, networking gear, fibre optic cables – that spans more than 100 countries.
In recent years, doubts have surfaced about how cloud platforms store data and whether they are truly secure.
British police decided to put some of their most sensitive data on the Microsoft platform in a 2017 meeting, a record of which was examined by the Guardian.
In doing so, officers accepted that “US government insiders” would be able to see the data, and that it could be “transmitted worldwide”, with “the extent of this … unknown”.
According to five specialists who reviewed the Guardian’s findings, the risks identified in that document persist today. Almost every UK police force now depends on Microsoft Azure, and the UK government spends at least £1.9bn on Microsoft software each year.
“There’s no evidence that this has been properly understood,” said one source who has held senior roles in UK policing. The data is “some of the most sensitive that exists”, he added. “You’re talking about information that, if it gets into the wrong hands, or if the information is incorrect, [means] people can get hurt or may die.”
When the Guardian approached the police about the possibility that sensitive information was not secure, they appeared to wave aside these risks, saying Britain’s contracts with Microsoft meant US authorities could not view data without express permission and that the data it stored on Microsoft remained in the UK.
These statements appeared to contradict public admissions by Microsoft, which said in a disclosure to Police Scotland in 2023 that data “can go outside the UK” and that it “cannot guarantee data sovereignty”.
Microsoft said it “does not provide any government with direct or unfettered access to customer data”, and that it had not provided UK data in response to a US government request. It added that, like all US-based tech companies, it responded to US government requests made through valid legal processes.
The threat of ‘US government insider attackers’
In 2017, a senior police oﬃcer, Ian Dyson, chaired a meeting in which stakeholders considered 15 risks the UK would face if police forces decided to transfer their data to Microsoft’s global cloud.
![Ian Dyson posing for a photo in his City of London police uniform](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/6d8e2daad2c1a3e55abafbbc8ff4edf51ef24c26/0_1169_2920_3953/master/2920.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
That meeting considered both the police’s use of Microsoft’s software, such as Office 365, and the reliance on the cloud that underpins these services, Azure. Those risks, and the resulting police decisions, were set out in a summary document seen by the Guardian and signed off by Dyson.
This was four years after the advent of a policy called “cloud first”. Introduced by the Cabinet Office in 2013, it became a government-wide effort to push almost all departments to migrate their data on to the “public cloud” – commercial offerings by tech companies, often based in the US. Departments that did not want to do this had to jump through burdensome administrative hoops.
Dyson was the police commissioner of the City of London at the time, but he held another title: senior information risk owner for all of Britain, or the SIRO. It was his job to set the norms for how British police could safely handle their data.
In their assessment, officers came to startling conclusions about what would happen if they put police data on Azure. Firstly, they considered it would be vulnerable to hackers: Microsoft’s software “carries vulnerabilities which will be exploited by cybercriminals and other threat actors in due course”.
Separately, it added: “Police forces cannot be certain where their data will be processed or stored.
“The hyper-scale and global nature of the Microsoft cloud means that police data, and metadata relating to police data could be transmitted and stored worldwide by Microsoft, and the extent of this will be unknown.”
The document specifically identified the potential risk from what it described as “US government insiders”. It said: “There is a risk of compromise of sensitive data shared by, or taken from, Microsoft by the US government being released by US government insider attackers.”
The document explained that the data intended for migration was sensitive. In fact, “a significant volume” of it exceeded the classification “oﬃcial”. In the UK, this suggests it was either “oﬃcial sensitive”, “secret”, or “top secret”.
The assessment also suggested Microsoft’s platform was unable to guarantee this data would be secure. “This places sensitive data, inadequately protected in an environment which then becomes a significantly more attractive target for attackers,” it said.
As well as risks, the report also listed mitigations. On the problem of cyber-attacks, it mandated that police servers should be repaired promptly, kept up to date and have antivirus software.
To address the risk of “US government insiders” and the concern that Microsoft might store UK policing data “worldwide” it suggested “applying Microsoft’s ‘out-of-the-box’ native encryption” and leaving the final decision about using Microsoft up to individual police chiefs.
Several experts interviewed by the Guardian, including cloud computing specialists and engineers working for Microsoft, suggested these mitigations were inadequate. Microsoft’s internal encryption does not prevent its employees accessing UK police data; nor would it stop the US government obtaining British policing files.
The National Police Chief’s Council (NPCC) said access to data stored on the cloud is limited to those with a genuine need to access it and that this is subject to strict controls. Despite that claim, a Microsoft engineer who reviewed the Guardian’s findings said the information “could be viewed by hundreds of people around the world, some of them not vetted, many of them not directly employed by Microsoft”.
Despite the risks identified by the assessment, every police force in the UK put its data, wholly or in part, on Microsoft’s cloud. Some began migrating their information in 2017. A few forces, such as Police Scotland, are still finalising their adoption of the technology.
The files cover the “full gamut of data: intelligence, body-worn video, digital evidence and case files, as well as the non-law enforcement data any organisation has”, said the source who held senior roles in UK policing.
‘We do not expect any sharing … without permission’
The UK government spends billions each year on services oﬀered by three US tech companies: Amazon, Google and Microsoft.
Up to 60% of its IT infrastructure is hosted on cloud platforms. Britain’s intelligence data is hosted on Amazon’s cloud services, as is its customs data. The Ministry of Defence uses Azure. There is “a deep dependency on US hyperscalers”, said Dave Michels, a researcher with the Cloud Legal Project, at Queen Mary University of London.
This is the result of 13 years of decisions like Dyson’s. It is unclear if the potential consequences are broadly understood.
When the Guardian approached the NPCC over the document signed by Dyson, it said: “UK policing as standard requires the use of UK-only datacentres,” but added that “on occasion” Microsoft employees could access the data “to provide support”.
Asked whether the US government could access the data, a police spokesperson said they could not comment on the phrase “US government insiders”, because “terminology … changes continuously” and the document was “outdated”.
“In line with the contract signed with Microsoft, we do not expect any sharing with the US government without the express permission of the UK government,” they added.
Microsoft said: “The suggestion that use of Microsoft cloud services means customer data is inherently insecure or automatically exposed to foreign governments is inaccurate.” It said it had “never provided UK government data in response to any US or global authority request”.
Two legal experts, as well as several Microsoft engineers who spoke anonymously to the Guardian, suggested these assertions did not give an accurate picture of the potential risks.
By default, Microsoft’s cloud was “a global network of datacentres”, said Michels. It had facilities on every continent and this meant, generally, that data stored on it was stored everywhere: pieces of a single file could be held across multiple countries, from Sweden to Ethiopia.
In recent years, Michels said, Microsoft had begun to offer clients in Europe greater assurances about where their data was stored, including assuring some customers that their data would remain within EU borders. But “the focus on data location is a bit of a red herring”, he said.
This was because thousands of engineers from more than 100 countries maintained Microsoft’s systems.
