title: Apple's new boss starts with gamble on costly new foldable iPhone
author: Kali Hays; Lily Jamali
content:
![An image of the new foldable iPhone Duo in a woman's hands, being opened like a book.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/569e/live/3eec7030-ac80-11f1-994b-c7df927931ed.png)
Critics say Apple has not meaningfully changed the design of the iPhone since its initial release in 2007
- Published
John Ternus has entered his second week as Apple's chief executive and the company has revealed the first major change to the iPhone since it was released almost 20 years ago.
Ternus, who took on Apple's top job after Tim Cook stepped down, was onstage on Wednesday at the company's annual product release event in front of huge images of the first foldable iPhone.
With a book-style format, the new iPhone, dubbed the Duo, is the largest ever size of the product. And with a US starting price of $1,999 (Â£1,475) going up to $3,200, it is also the most expensive. UK prices start at Â£1,999.
Ternus said the Duo was "inspired by the iPad" but called the folding features "fluid and completely intuitive."
The foldable phone has been a work-in-progress inside Apple for several years.
When unfolded, the new Duo has the look of a small iPad. When folded in half, it has the look of a wider iPhone.
Ternus said during the event that Apple wanted to avoid the look and feel of other foldable smart phones on the market, which he said "feel like two phones stuck together... making a larger screen feel much smaller."
The Duo, he said, is the "result of a series of remarkable innovations that we think will redefine the experience of using a foldable phone."
Ternus was directly involved in developing the foldable iPhone as he spent many years as a top executive inside Apple's hardware division before being tapped earlier this year as Cook's successor.
![The folding iPhone](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1040/cpsprodpb/b448/live/bef178c0-ac85-11f1-ab14-5b9069dc795d.png)
The new foldable iPhone can operate in two forms.
Ben Wood, chief analyst at technology research firm FDM, said it was likely Ternus's promotion was timed specifically "to coincide with what will be arguably one of the biggest iPhone launches for many years".
"Nothing happens by accident at Apple," Wood added.
Carolina Milanesi, an analyst at Creative Strategies who attended the Wednesday presentation, said the spotlight on Ternus made it feel "almost like he was a product himself."
Altering the design of the iPhone may address some criticism that Apple has yet to land a major product hit or truly exciting innovation since the first iPhone came out in 2007.
"The foldable risks becoming a premium-priced ornament in the portfolio, imparting badge value but not meaningful growth," said Dipanjan Chatterjee, an analyst at Forrester.
Previously, the highest starting price of the newest iPhone was $900 (Â£664). Apple also revealed on Wednesday the new iPhone 18 and 18 Pro, which start at $1,200 (Â£885) and $1,300 (Â£959) respectively.
Chatterjee said the foldable iPhone could go the way of Apple's Vision Pro headset, which the company priced at $3,699 (Â£2,729) and has not been a hit with buyers. Or, he said, it could be the company's next Apple Watch which, while not as popular as the iPhone, is bought by millions of people each year.
The way people have become accustomed to the way the iPhone operates is another potential hurdle to Apple seeing big sales of the new design.
"Foldables are interesting devices", Milanesi noted. "A lot of people are intrigued by it, but the software and the learning curve that you have from moving from a traditional phone to a foldable is real."
![Hands holding the folding iPhone like a book, with messages on one side and images on the other.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1248/cpsprodpb/7339/live/320a0a70-ac86-11f1-ab14-5b9069dc795d.png)
Wood noted that the current market for foldable smartphones from the likes of Samsung and Huawei make up only 2% of smartphone sales. Even with Apple's version likely driving interest and demand, sales are only expected to reach 4% of the total market in the next decade, according to data and analytics firm FDM.
The iPhone has been Apple's top-selling product and accounts for more than half of the company's sales each year.
In recent quarters, the company has boasted that the iPhone is more in-demand than ever, with the most recent version of the device becoming its most successful product launch.
The company also revealed more about the coming relaunch of its audio and chat assistant Siri, which it now calls Siri AI.
Starting with the iPhone 18, the bot will now be able to go across information on a person's phone, like messages and emails, to find information, answer queries and take action on a person's behalf.
Some Siri AI features will also be available on the new Apple Watch, including the ability to take notes of conversations and transcribe them, should a wearer enable that feature.
Ternus referred to new AI-enabled capabilities on the iPhone as an "intelligent personal hub", and admitted that Apple would be making use of "the most private details of your daily life."
He insisted that all of it will remain private, with the AI features often running "on device", meaning not through third-party companies. And when a third-party is required for a function, Ternus said it will remain private in a remote server, or cloud.
"Others see that data as something to collect and store", Ternus said. "Here, not even Apple can access what's yours."
summary: John Ternus has started his second week as Apple's chief executive by unveiling the company's first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, at an annual product release event. The book-style device is Apple's largest and most expensive iPhone to date, with a starting price of $1,999 in the US. Alongside the Duo, Apple introduced the iPhone 18 series and new AI-enabled features for Siri, while analysts remain divided on whether the costly foldable phone will drive meaningful growth.
key_points: John Ternus revealed the foldable iPhone Duo during his second week as Apple's chief executive, following Tim Cook's departure.
The iPhone Duo features a book-style folding format with a US starting price of $1,999, making it Apple's largest and most expensive iPhone.
Apple also announced the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro, along with an upgraded Siri AI assistant designed to access on-device information privately.
Analysts have expressed mixed views on the Duo, warning it could either struggle with high pricing like the Vision Pro or succeed like the Apple Watch.

title: Sony can’t support a PS6 home and portable console warns ex-PlayStation boss
author: Michael Beckwith
content:
![Someone playing a PS5 video game on their PlayStation Portal handheld](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_311309513-4eab.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Ex-PlayStation boss Shawn Layden doesn’t think the PlayStation 6 having home console and handheld models is a good idea.
If you haven’t been keeping up with PlayStation 6 rumours, the most popular one is that Sony plans on offering two different consoles: a traditional home console and a handheld version.
The jury’s still out on whether the handheld would function exactly like a Nintendo Switch, but comments by Sony Entertainment CEO Hideaki Nishino, about experiences ‘beyond the living room’, do lend credence to the handheld’s existence.
As a handheld it’s speculated it will only be compatible with PlayStation 5 games, but former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden feels that Sony will be unable to juggle two very different consoles.
The prospect of the rumoured handheld was brought up in an interview with Reiss ‘Kiwi Talkz’ Reilly on YouTube, where Layden bluntly says, ‘the company really struggles to sell two different pieces of hardware at the same time.’
Layden is basing this on his own experiences trying to sell the PlayStation Portable (PSP), which was available around the same time as the PlayStation 3.
Expert, exclusive gaming analysis
While the PSP was very successful for Sony, at least in Japan, the PlayStation 3 saw a much rougher launch and isn’t as fondly remembered, being almost outsold by the Xbox 360.
‘‘But what about PlayStation Portable? That was a real success.’ Yes, and while we were doing that, I was struggling selling PlayStation 3,’ acknowledges Layden.
This is not an entirely apt comparison as the PSP and PlayStation 3 offered bespoke games you couldn’t get on either console, whereas the two hypothetical next gen consoles will share the same library (assuming the PlayStation 6 is backwards compatible).
However, Layden also argues that Sony would be hampered by needing to split time and resources between the two consoles.
‘It’s not just development resources; it’s also marketing resources. You almost have to set up two different companies to do it, where neither one is worried about what the other one is doing, they’re just trying to be successful in their own right,’ explains Layden.
‘Because when you have one company managing both, inevitably there’s stealing from Peter to pay Paul for something else, and ‘Well, we’ll move that marketing program over to this other game which is going to be more successful than that game was.’
- 
	![Saban delivers the plot twist on Four In A Bed](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_311213074-4705.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=158px%2C0px%2C730px%2C410px&resize=646%2C363)
- Nigella Lawson's first Bake Off episode is one of the most disastrous openers ever
- Mo Gilligan makes Andi Peters joke at NTAs after backlash against Miriam Margolyes
- ITV sets record straight over claim Sir Tom Jones is exiting The Voice UK
‘All the trade-offs just sort of… you lose your focus on what you’re really trying to get done here.’
While the PlayStation Portal handheld device can run PlayStation 5 games, it does so by streaming them from a nearby PlayStation 5 console, which is very different to running games natively.
Although Layden is right in what he says in terms of a separate handheld, that would play its own games, the only scenario that makes any real sense, given current technology and prices, is a portable PlayStation 5, with many speculating that the PlayStation 5’s new power saver graphic mode is primarily designed with the new portable in mind.
It’s less obvious what’s going on with the PlayStation 6 home console but if that was a more modest upgrade, akin to the PS5 Pro, with no exclusive games, it wouldn’t be a surprise.
![Mock-up of a PlayStation 6 console with PlayStation 5 controller](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_311310538-0db8.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646)

To submit Inbox letters and Reader’s Features more easily, without the need to send an email, just use our Submit Stuff page here.
For more stories like this, check our Gaming page.
summary: Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has warned that Sony would struggle to simultaneously support both a home console and a handheld version of the rumoured PlayStation 6. Drawing on his experience selling the PSP alongside the PlayStation 3, Layden argues that managing two hardware platforms splits crucial development and marketing resources. He believes this division ultimately leads to a loss of focus and compromises the success of the products.
key_points: Rumours suggest Sony might release both a traditional home console and a handheld version for the PlayStation 6 generation.
Ex-PlayStation boss Shawn Layden argues that Sony struggles to successfully sell two different pieces of hardware simultaneously.
Layden points to his past experience managing the PlayStation Portable and the PlayStation 3 as evidence of the challenges involved.
Split resources for development and marketing between two consoles can lead to a loss of focus and internal competition.

title: "Modern, musical, luxurious" – Marantz's compact streaming system with CD player is elevated in every way
author: Kashfia Kabir
content:
![Marantz MCR 60n DAB](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/zaUjqG3UyMbLwyShWfyLRg.jpg) 
We're rather fond of Marantz's Melody (MCR) compact systems that combine CD player, radio, amplification and network streaming into one stylish box. Previous models in the range – such as the M-CR610 and M-CR603 – nabbed What Hi-Fi? Award wins for their user-friendly design, breadth of features and enjoyable sound.
The new Marantz MCR 60n DAB aims to keep that same compact concept going, but is now a much more elevated affair, with plenty of new features, a classy design, and a new price.
The MCR 60n DAB continues to feature a CD player, DAB/FM radio, Bluetooth and AirPlay 2, and it is now joined by a moving magnet phono stage owing to turntables’ continuing popularity.
The system is powered by Marantz's HEOS streaming platform, which brings with it support for popular music streaming apps, which include Tidal Connect, Qobuz Connect and Spotify Connect. There is also an optical input and a 3.5mm headphone output.
 ![Marantz MCR 60n DAB](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/P5Y5VjNLLDjaQCrrL25qaL.png) 
Hi-res streaming support has been extended to 32-bit/384kHz PCM and DSD 11.2 MHz, while low-latency LE Audio and two-way Bluetooth is also on board. It's Roon Ready, too.
For seamless TV audio playback, it now boasts an HDMI eARC input, which supports 7.1 channels and Dolby Digital/Dolby Digital Plus decoding via built-in DSP, and can play up to 24-bit/192kHz PCM audio.
These are substantial feature gains over the previous model, the four-star M-CR612 (also called Melody X) that we reviewed in 2019. The HEOS platform and app has been updated since, with Marantz saying the onboarding set-up process should be even better than before.
The latest hi-fi, home cinema and tech news, reviews, buying advice and deals, direct to your inbox.
The sound quality has been improved, too. There is an updated power supply for higher and more stable current delivery, while the power rating has been increased to 65W per channel (into 4 ohms) from a previous 50W. Marantz says the extra headroom will result in better power delivery and better sound quality overall from the Class D amplifier. Additionally, there are new custom components in the circuitry to further help deliver a clean, powerful and low-noise performance.
 ![Marantz MCR 60n DAB](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Ge9shvvWRgUr38HKLYQsog.jpg) 
The bottom chassis of the unit features an additional plate to help reduce vibrations coming from the CD mechanism, while the feet have a high density structure and felt cushioning to also help with damping and deliver a more stable bass performance.
The MCR 60n DAB can also be used as a preamp or with active speakers thanks to fixed and variable outputs, while the subwoofer output now has adjustable crossover filters in 10Hz increments from 30Hz to 250Hz.
The unit is also compatible with Dirac Live Room Correction, although you'll need to buy a license separately to make full use of the calibration software.
A new feature is the ability to save four 'Smart Selects' that store your favourite sound configuration for a certain source. For instance, you may want to employ different volume and tone settings and a Dirac-calibrated profile for when watching TV/movie content compared with listening to music via streaming or from radio, and this lets you choose your pre-set sound profiles accordingly.
These can be easily accessed from the button on the unit itself, or by using the updated remote control.
 ![Marantz MCR 60n DAB](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/fbvuv45cwV3qBA9e2srhLg.jpg) 
The design of the MCR 60n DAB is inspired by the Marantz Model M1, with a more minimal and luxurious design than before, but it retains the same compact footprint.
The Marantz MCR 60n DAB will be available for £800 / €900 from 15th September. This DAB version is for the European market and is available in Champagne Gold and Black finishes, while the non-DAB version will be available for $1000 in the black finish only.
That's a substantial jump in price over the previous M-CR612, which we tested at £630 in 2019, while older MCR units tended to cost £500. With all the new features and proposed improvements for the MCR 60n DAB, we're hoping it will be more than justified.

During her time in the consumer tech industry, she has reviewed hundreds of products (including speakers, amplifiers, turntables and headphones), been to countless trade shows across the world and fallen in love with hi-fi kit much bigger than her. title: Apple expected to unveil folding iPhone as new CEO takes center stage
author: Johana Bhuiyan
content:
All eyes are on Apple’s annual fall announcement of new products this afternoon, where the company is expected to unveil the most significant change to the iPhone since the smartphone’s introduction in 2007.
Unlike previous iterations, the new iPhone is expected to fold, opening and closing like a passport to double its screen size.
The product release event, titled “Surprise and Shine”, begins at 10am Pacific Standard Time on Apple’s campus in Cupertino, California, south of San Francisco.
While competitors have released foldable smartphones since the late 2010s, the new model will be a first for the iPhone maker and will also serve as the first big test for the company’s new CEO, John Ternus, who assumed the role on 1 September.
Apple is expected to price the phone north of $2000, more than what some of its competitors charge for their foldable phones. A Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, for instance, retails for $1899. Much remains unknown about Apple’s device, including its name, though it is rumored to be named either the iPhone Fold or the iPhone Ultra.
Apple reportedly began testing prototypes of its folding iPhone display in early 2021 – though at the time there were no plans for its launch, according to a Bloomberg report. Ultimately, the phone the company is rumored to launch will be about 5.5in when it’s closed and 7.8in when it opens. It’s also not expected to have Face ID because the device is too thin to hold the camera that would enable the facial recognition scan. Reports indicate it will only offer Touch ID instead.
Apple is also expected to make several more routine announcements, including new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max models. Though the foldable iPhone may take center stage Wednesday, demand for foldable phones makes up only a small sliver of overall mobile device sales. Customers’ interest in standard iPhones, by contrast, remains high, as evidenced in Apple’s most recent robust earnings.
The company is also expected to unveil new iterations of some of its other product offerings at its events and over the next few months, including updates to its Apple Watch and AirPods lines, according to Bloomberg, as well as its first-ever touchscreen MacBook.
Ternus will take the stage as CEO for the first time and mark the beginning of his tenure as the head of Apple, replacing outgoing CEO Tim Cook. In a note to employees on his first day, Ternus said that he was excited about “the incredible products already in the works and the ones we haven’t even imagined”.
after newsletter promotion
“I’m honored to be stepping into this role at what is truly the greatest company in the world, and I am so excited about everything we have in store,” Ternus wrote in his letter. “We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal. Thanks for everything you’ve all done to make it possible.”
summary: Apple is expected to unveil its first-ever folding iPhone at its annual fall product event in Cupertino, California. The new device, expected to be priced above $2,000, will feature Touch ID instead of Face ID and measures about 5.5 inches closed and 7.8 inches open. The event also marks the debut of John Ternus as Apple's new CEO following Tim Cook's departure.
key_points: Apple's fall event is expected to feature the debut of the company's first folding iPhone.
The new folding phone is rumored to cost over $2,000 and will use Touch ID instead of Face ID.
John Ternus will lead his first major product event as Apple's new CEO, replacing Tim Cook.
Apple is also expected to announce iPhone 18 Pro models, updates to Apple Watch and AirPods, and its first touchscreen MacBook.

title: Pixel 11 review: Google sets the bar for standard flagship phones
author: Samuel Gibbs
content:
Google’s Pixel 11 continues to set the standard for what you should expect from the base model of a flagship phone with class-leading cameras, long software support and almost all the bells and whistles of its most expensive phones.
The regular Pixel 11 costs £879 (€999/$899/A$1,499) making it £80 or equivalent more expensive than last year’s model as the cost of RAMageddon continues to bite. It’s not cheap by any stretch of the imagination, but it comes with 256GB of storage and is £200 less than the Pixel 11 Pro, matching rival Samsung’s Galaxy S26.
At a glance the Pixel 11 looks very similar to the previous two Google phone iterations: glass front and back with flat aluminium sides and large pill-shaped bar at the back, which is much slimmer this time. Stick it in a case and the protruding camera all but disappears.
![The camera bar of the Google Pixel 11.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/3c24e0aace32b9edcbf995ab194659ec81dee45f/1855_633_3904_3123/master/3904.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The 6.3in OLED screen is crisp and super bright with up to a 120Hz refresh rate to keep your scrolling smooth. The in-screen fingerprint scanner is fast and accurate, while the camera-based face recognition works well during the day and is secure enough for use with banking apps, unlike similar systems on most Android rivals.
Specifications
- 
  Screen: 6.3in 120Hz FHD+ OLED (422ppi)
- 
  Processor: Google Tensor G6
- 
  RAM: 12GB
- 
  Storage: 256 or 512GB
- 
  Operating system: Android 17
- 
  Camera: 48MP+ 13MP UW + 10.8MP 5x tele; 10.5MP selfie
- 
  Connectivity: 5G, eSIM, wifi 6E, UWB, NFC, Bluetooth 6 and GNSS
- 
  Water resistance: IP68 (1.5m for 30 minutes)
- 
  Dimensions: 152.8 x 72.0 x 8.6mm
- 
  Weight: 197g
Faster and more efficient Tensor G6 chip
![The USB-C port of the Google Pixel 11.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/551f13830607c31f11dcbe592c644797839fc52b/2137_1100_2742_2194/master/2742.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The Pixel has a new generation of Google’s chip, the Tensor G6, which is up to 20% faster in tests. It significantly lags top-end rivals from Qualcomm and Apple, so won’t win any raw performance awards, but feels snappy in daily tasks and can handle mid-level gaming just fine.
The battery life is also improved over previous models, lasting about 54 hours of light use between charges. That includes actively using the screen for more than seven hours for browsing, messaging, apps and photos across a mix of 5G and wifi.
Gaming and more demanding use hits the battery harder, but the Pixel should be able to see out even the heaviest of use days.
Android 17 with more proactive AI
![Screenshots from a Google Pixel 11 series showing Magic Cue’s proactive assistance in the messages app.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b1e23f71dba5dcbfc5509f674868e28d8fe58aa9/0_0_5413_2424/master/5413.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The Pixel 11 runs the latest Android 17 out of the box with operating system and security updates provided until August 2033.
The software is slick, nicely animated and well optimised, with plenty of colourful customisation if you want it. As with previous Pixels, it is a showcase for some of Google’s most advanced AI systems, many of which run on-device, making them fast.
The most interesting of the tools remains Google’s proactive AI systems, which vary a bit depending on where you live. In the UK the expanded Magic Cue from last year pops up in messages and a few other apps with information such as your schedule, flight or order details, and suggestions for good local restaurants from Google maps or photos to share in a chat. In the US, Canada, Australia and a few other regions, the feature is called “Gemini Proactive Assistance” but has similar powers. If you use a supported app, such as Google Messages, the suggestions are low-key great. Unfortunately it doesn’t work in WhatsApp, Signal or other third-party apps I’ve tried, which limits its usefulness.
In the UK and US, Gemini can go further, proactively taking action for you, such as booking a restaurant via OpenTable, which is the type of assistance that has long been promised by various AI agents.
Another useful AI feature is built directly into Google’s keyboard called Rambler, which is voice typing on steroids. You can speak naturally to it and the system will remove your ums and ers and other deviations to produce a succinct, fully formed sentence or paragraph. It makes trying to dictate a rushed messaged while hustling for public transport a lot easier, although it doesn’t show your text until after you hit the stop button, unlike most other dictation tools.
Camera
![The camera app on a Google Pixel 11 shooting a garden scene.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/df6f72af54dc442c24d7288e5526405c13a428e7/1742_1108_3345_2676/master/3345.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The Pixel 11 has three cameras on the back and a solid 10.5-megapixel selfie camera in the screen.
The improved main 48MP camera captures excellent photos across a range of lighting conditions, including low light where its larger sensor helps capture more of what’s available. The 13MP ultra-wide camera is one of the best on a phone of this class, helpful for fitting more in the shot or providing a different perspective. But it is the 10.8MP 5x telephoto camera that sets it apart from the competition, capable of meaningfully closing the distance to objects. In bright light it can digitally zoom to 30x magnification with surprisingly good results.
Entirely new for the Pixel camera this year is the “Looks” feature, which allows you to customise how the phone captures and processes your photos for very different styles far beyond simple filters applied after the fact.
There are three versions of the default look available – natural, vanilla and shadows – plus six more-distinctive looks, including “digi” that replicates the look of the old digital cameras that has recently become popular. Each look can be customised in colour, tone, grain and sharpness, so you can get arty or replicate a particular film style.
If you are a Pixel user who has ever thought its photos look a little too cold, dramatic or overly processed, this is for you.
The Pixel shoots great video at up to 4K at 60 frames a second. The new Magic Capture feature is a one-button shooting mode that records video and photos automatically that is best used during events such as birthday parties where you want to be more in the moment but still capture the scene.
Google has also added a “Creator Suite” mode to the video capture, which shoots straight to a folder you can quickly storyboard and trim to create a video. It also has a teleprompter mode for shooting face to camera, a social media grid to get the alignment correct and speech enhancement that cuts out background noise.
All these features are in addition to Google’s popular Auto Best Take, Add Me and Camera Coach from last year, which makes the new Pixel camera one of the most feature rich available.
Sustainability
![The back of the Google Pixel 11.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/9e8cd7a90efb5c062966c9c8263a5c25aa59a72d/1091_587_4764_3811/master/4764.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The battery is rated to last in excess of 1,000 full charge cycles with at least 80% of its original capacity. The phone is repairable by Google, third-party shops or self-repair with manuals and parts available.
The Pixel 11 is contains 33% recycled materials by weight. The company breaks down the phone’s environmental impact in its report and will recycle old devices for free.
Price
The Google Pixel 11 costs from £879 (€999/$899/A$1,499) in a choice of four colours.
For comparison, the Pixel 10a costs £499, the Pixel 11 Pro costs £1,079, the Pixel 11 Pro XL costs £1,279, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold costs from £1,799, the Samsung Galaxy S26 costs £879 and the Apple iPhone 17 costs £799.
Verdict
The Pixel 11 isn’t the most advanced Google phone, nor is it the cheapest. But this middle-ground model offers more than enough to beat the competition and question whether you really need to spend more on a Pro phone.
It offers, yet again, a very high-quality experience, great triple camera, long software support and very good battery life. It won’t win any raw performance awards, so those looking for a gaming phone should look elsewhere, but it feels fast and responsive in daily use.
Google’s AI tools are second to none, particularly its Rambler dictation feature in the keyboard and the proactive Gemini features, which offer genuinely useful help even if they are not available in every third-party app.
The new camera looks feature provides more control over photos than ever before on a Pixel, so you can tailor it to your preferences or get creative far beyond simple filters.
It may not have changed all that much from last year’s equally excellent Pixel 10, and it isn’t quite the bargain the Pixel 10a is, but the Pixel 11 is the best phone you can get under £900.
 Pros: seven years of software updates, great camera with 5x telephoto, great screen, impressive local AI features, Qi2.2 wireless charging and magnetic accessory support, long battery life, good size, fast fingerprint and face recognition, 256GB starting storage.
Cons: face unlock option not as secure as Face ID, raw performance short of rivals, no physical SIM card slot in the US, heavier than rivals, not a big upgrade on previous model, no wifi 7.
![The fingerprint scanner in the screen of the Google Pixel 11.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/66c393d09c577fabc37f2c37509072c1bff9ce14/1080_422_4848_3878/master/4848.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
summary: The Google Pixel 11 is a flagship smartphone priced starting at £879 (€999/$899/A$1,499) that features a crisp 6.3-inch OLED screen, a faster Tensor G6 processor, and long battery life. It stands out with a versatile triple-camera system, extensive AI integration, and software support guaranteed until August 2033. While it lags behind top rivals in raw gaming performance, it offers a high-quality experience that competes strongly against more expensive pro models.
key_points: Starts at £879 with 256GB of storage and runs on Android 17 with software support through August 2033.
Features a 6.3-inch 120Hz OLED screen, faster Tensor G6 chip, and a battery lasting about 54 hours of light use.
Includes a powerful triple-camera system featuring a 48MP main sensor, 13MP ultra-wide, and a 10.8MP 5x telephoto lens.
Integrates advanced AI tools such as proactive Gemini assistance and the Rambler voice typing keyboard feature.
Constructed with 33% recycled materials and offers an improved repairable design.

title: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images
author: Jay Peters
content:
OpenAI announced ChatGPT Images 2.5 on Tuesday and is adding a new way to tell ChatGPT what you want it to make an image of: by drawing a doodle. With a new feature called Sketch, you can just draw something right inside ChatGPT and then tell ChatGPT how you want it to make an image based on that sketch.
ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images
OpenAI’s updated image generation tools in ChatGPT let you use a doodle as part of your prompt.
![ai-label (1)](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/ai-label-1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
![ai-label (1)](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/ai-label-1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
You can activate the Sketch feature by typing @Sketch into your chat box, and a window will pop up where you can make your drawing. I briefly tested it, and it successfully turned my bad doodle of a cat that I drew with my computer mouse into a realistic photo, per my instructions. You can also now leave comments directly on parts of images that you want changed, which I used to make the cat’s eyes green instead of blue.
![Screenshots of ChatGPT making a cat image based off of a sketch.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-08-at-1.08.36-PM.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
As for ChatGPT Images 2.5, OpenAI says that it makes images with “more natural lighting and richer textures,” is better at following your editing instructions “across multiple turns,” and that image generation latency has been reduced by “up to 50% compared with Images 2.0.” ChatGPT Images 2.5 is out now for ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex users on desktop, mobile, and web, according to OpenAI.
summary: OpenAI has announced ChatGPT Images 2.5 and introduced a new feature called Sketch, which allows users to generate detailed AI images using a doodle as part of their prompt. Users can activate Sketch by typing @Sketch in the chat box, and they can also leave comments directly on generated images to request specific changes. The updated Images 2.5 model features more natural lighting, richer textures, improved multi-turn editing, and up to 50 percent lower latency.
key_points: OpenAI announced ChatGPT Images 2.5 and the Sketch feature.
Sketch allows users to draw a doodle inside ChatGPT and use it as a prompt to generate detailed AI images.
Users can type @Sketch to open the drawing window.
Users can leave direct comments on specific parts of images to request edits, such as changing eye color.
ChatGPT Images 2.5 delivers more natural lighting, richer textures, and up to 50 percent reduced latency compared to Images 2.0.

title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT Images 2.5 with 'sharper details' and 'more precise editing' - 9to5Mac
author: Zac Hall
content:
![](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/06/chatgpt-orange.webp?w=1600) 
In April, OpenAI released upgraded image generation technology with ChatGPT Images 2. Five months later, the company is releasing an enhanced version, ChatGPT Images 2.5.
ChatGPT Images 2 was a notable leap over the company’s earlier image generation tools.
It added 2K resolution output, multiple aspect ratio support, and the ability to use web research for up-to-date information. Images 2 also added non-Latin language expertise and two intelligence levels: Instant and Thinking.
The latest Images 2.5 version touts “sharper details, faster generation, more precise editing, and better tools for creating and sharing.”
“Images 2.5 produces more natural lighting and richer textures, is better at preserving the subjects in your reference photos, and follows editing instructions more reliably across multiple turns,” OpenAI says.
“We’ve also reduced image generation latency by up to 50% compared with Images 2.0, so you can generate images and refine your concepts more quickly.”
Additionally, the company details a new “Sketch” feature that enables drawing directly in ChatGPT. This can be used as a reference for image generation. Plus OpenAI is introducing templates for popular image formats, prompt sharing for others to try your ideas related to image-gen, and more.
Additionally, OpenAI is releasing two versions of Images 2.5 for developers to build around in their apps. GPT-Image-2.5 Flare and GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburt will be available through OpenAI’s API:
GPT‑Image‑2.5 Flare brings the same improvements in quality, editing, and speed to the API and is the default choice for most applications, delivering higher-quality images than GPT‑Image‑2 at 50% lower latency. It’s well suited to everything from creator and social content to product experiences, visual search, rapid image prototyping, and high-volume generation.
GPT‑Image‑2.5 Sunburst is built for premium visual workflows that benefit from tighter control across edits. Use it for creative and editing workflows like production-ready campaign creative or polished product imagery.
“Images 2.5 is rolling out today to ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex users across all tiers on desktop, mobile, and web,” according to OpenAI. You can learn more about the new image-gen technology here.
Today’s ChatGPT Images 2.5 release follows last week’s GPT-6 Astra launch.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 worldwide unlock times revealed, and Xbox owners can seemingly still use the old New Zealand trick to play early
author: Sherif Saed
content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 arrives 19th November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. Depending on where you may be in the world, however, when you actually get to play varies.
Starting with PS5, GTA 6 has 15 different regional launch times. If you pre-ordered a digital copy through the PlayStation Store, the game's unlock time will be dictated by your account's region and store. In other words, it won't unlock for everyone at the same time.
GTA fansite GTAVice.net rifled through PlayStation Store data to uncover the full list of launch times across its 15 regions. The unlock times range between 11am UTC on 18th November at the earliest, to 6am UTC on 19th November - a 19-hour difference.
As is common with staggered releases, New Zealand goes first. GTA 6 becomes playable there at 12am NZDT on 19th November (midnight on 18th November). Mexico, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua are the last to gain access, where the game unlocks at 12am CST on 20th November (midnight on 19th November).
Notably, the release timestamps don't appear on the PlayStation Store pages for every country with a PS Store page. GTAVice lists Bahrain, China, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman and Qatar as all missing that information. For countries like The Philippines, Russia, Serbia and Vietnam their store pages instead redirect you to other countries' stores.
It's worth reiterating that your unlock time is tied to the PlayStation Store's account region, not where you physically are in the world. For instance, if you reside in Canada but made your digital pre-order on the UK store, the game will unlock for you when it does for everyone in the UK.
We actually got reminded of that regional split shortly after pre-orders went live for the code-in-box "physical" version of the game, as multiple retailers issued warnings that codes are region-locked. Rockstar later clarified which countries are affected, and which codes can only be redeemed in the country they were bought.
Things are more interesting on Xbox, however, as the console platform allows users to switch regions and stores through the system menu, meaning copies aren't locked to any particular region. As anyone who's done that trick to play Call of Duty games early each year knows, of course, changing your region to New Zealand is all you need to play GTA 6 as soon as humanly possible.
summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 is scheduled to release on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, featuring 15 different regional launch times for PS5 digital pre-orders. Because unlock times are tied to account regions, PlayStation players cannot easily bypass their local times. However, Xbox owners can reportedly still use the system menu region-switch trick to play the game early via New Zealand.
key_points: GTA 6 releases on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
PlayStation 5 digital pre-orders feature 15 different regional launch times spanning a 19-hour difference.
PlayStation unlock times are strictly tied to the account's store region rather than the player's physical location.
Xbox owners can use the traditional New Zealand region-switch trick to play the game early.

title: Some people are worried Apple's folding iPhone design could present a brand new health risk
author: Daniel John
content:
![iPhone Ultra render](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/yRjhKbdFpwpWMbenMSnUud.png) 
Ah, the iPhone Ultra. Or iPhone Fold. Or iPhone Flip. Whatever it's going to be called, the folding iPhone is very much rumoured to be arriving this week, finally giving us a proper look at the most on-again-off-again tech product of the last five years. But while many are simply excited to learn more about the design and specs, others are begging: won't somebody think of the thumbs?
You've heard of 'iPhone pinky'; whereby one's little finger becomes sore as a result of resting a phone on it during a session of doomscrolling. But according to one physical therapist, the extra weight of the so-called iPhone Ultra could be bad news for our thumbs.
 ![iPhone Ultra concept](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/kwNxuAapwkMdseanfkn5HZ.jpg) 
Leaks suggest the foldable iPhone could weigh up to 78g more than the standard iPhone 17 when folded, with the extra weight ramping up strain on users' hands. Musculoskeletal physical therapist Martin Ratcliffe recently told mobile phone recycling comparison site Compare and Recycle about what this means for your hands:
“After several hours of use, the continued strain from the added weight can lead to fatigue and increase tension on the tissues, particularly the tissue around the thumb, which is the main finger used to navigate devices. Furthermore, the grip position may change because of the phone's foldable design. Overall, although the additional weight may be small, the repetitive strain and low-grade tension may lead to further stress and injury to surrounding tissues and joints.”
 ![best fold phones](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/tcm8iKC9QMuEGZas97jhhB.jpg) 
This all might sound a little alarmist, but there's precedent for foldable phone users complaining about hand strain. On a Reddit page for Samsung Galaxy Fold owners, users have asked whether others have experiencing aching or stinging hands.
Martin says to take breaks every 30-45 minutes to reduce the risk of tendon and muscle strains: “During these breaks, I recommend people put the phone down and look away to ensure a proper rest. People should stretch their palms and shake their hands for a few seconds to promote increased blood flow. Stretching each digit supports muscle repair and reduces tension.”

Daniel John is Design Editor at Creative Bloq. He reports on the worlds of design, branding and lifestyle tech, and has covered several industry events including Milan Design Week, OFFF Barcelona and Adobe Max in Los Angeles. He has interviewed leaders and designers at brands including Apple, Microsoft and Adobe. Daniel's debut book of short stories and poems was published in 2018, and his comedy newsletter is a Substack Bestseller.

summary: Rumors suggest that Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone may weigh up to 78g more than standard models, raising concerns among physical therapists about potential hand and thumb strain. Prolonged use and altered grip positions due to the foldable design could lead to fatigue, tissue tension, and repetitive strain injuries. Experts recommend taking breaks every 30 to 45 minutes to rest, stretch palms, and shake hands to promote blood flow and reduce muscle tension.
key_points: Apple's rumored folding iPhone could weigh up to 78g more than the standard iPhone 17.
Physical therapist Martin Ratcliffe warns the extra weight and new grip positions may increase strain and injury risk for thumbs.
Samsung Galaxy Fold owners have previously reported hand aching and stinging on Reddit.
Experts recommend taking breaks every 30 to 45 minutes, stretching palms, and shaking hands to prevent tendon and muscle strains.

title: Children reporting naked image sextortion scams 'more than double'
author: Luke Alsford; Keir Starmer
content:
![Close up of a girl using cell phone.](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/PRI_67097133-4484.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
The number of children who have reported being preyed on in sextortion cases has more than doubled, the NSPCC has warned.
The children’s charity revealed a surge in reports of kids being blackmailed with threats of the release of their nude images for money.
The new data is being released as the government deadline for Big Tech companies to implement nudity blocking technology for children on all smartphones and tablets expires today.
Andy Burnham is facing calls to quickly honour Sir Keir Starmer’s pledge to legislate to force Apple and Google to enforce the device-level safeguards.
In new data shared exclusively with Metro, the NSPCC said contacts with its Childline service about financially motivated sexual extortion (sextortion) had more than doubled in a year.
Of the 2,444 counselling sessions about online child sexual abuse and exploitation, between April 2025 and March 2026, 242 cases mentioned sextortion.
![EMBARGOED TO 0001 TUESDAY AUGUST 24 File photo dated 04/03/17 of a child using a laptop computer. The number of online grooming crimes recorded by police has risen sharply in the last three years, the NSPCC warned as it urged the Government to strengthen its plans for internet regulation. Issue date: Monday August 24, 2021. Figures obtained by the NSPCC from 42 police forces across England and Wales showed the number of recorded offences involving sexual communication with a child had increased by 69% since 2018. The charity said design flaws on social media platforms are being exploited by offenders, enabling younger users to be targeted, and the Government???s draft Online Safety Bill ??? introducing regulation to the sector ??? needs to go further in order to match the scale of the issue. See PA story TECHNOLOGY Grooming. Photo credit should read: Dominic Lipinski/PA Wire](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/PRI_196038499-b443.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
This is twice the number of sextortion scams reported to Childline in 2024/25, which sat at 120.
Childline dealt with 103 sextortion cases reported in 2023/4.
The NSPCC said that a large proportion of cases they came across involved male victims aged 14 to 17, who had been tricked into sending naked images to criminals.
Some young people revealed that they’d already sent money to a perpetrator – hoping that this would resolve the issue and that they would be left alone – only to be hit with further demands.
This included demands to pay a higher ransom or, in some cases, demands to pay in regular instalments.
Criminals were threatening to expose children’s naked images if they did not pay sums ranging from £20 to as much as £3,000.
Many young people are also tricked by fake profiles made by criminals posing as people they know.
‘They feel completely helpless’
![Rani Govender from NSPCC Linkedin https://www.linkedin.com/posts/alexanderwgray_nspcc-childline-huwedwards-activity-7241834541475147776-30pu](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_311202098-2e94.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=640) 
Rani Govender, the NSPCC’s Head of Child Safety Online, told Metro: ‘This is a very real concern impacting children in the UK.
‘Sextortion is incredibly distressing for children. When they get in contact with Childline, they feel completely helpless.
‘We know this can have such a devastating toll on children, which is why we are so focused on stopping this happening in the first place.’
The NSPCC has already revealed that of the 2,444 Childline sessions about online child sexual abuse and exploitation, more than 1,000 mentioned non-financial blackmail and threats to share intimate images of children.
This more typically involves female victims and demands that they share more images or meet criminals, although this is not always the case.
The NSPCC and other campaigners have warned that a new law to force tech companies to block nude imagery on a child’s device is the best way to stop children falling victim to sextortion scams.
One of Sir Keir’s last acts as Prime Minister was to order big tech companies to implement device-level protections to stop children taking, receiving or viewing nude images.
He gave firms like Apple and Google three months – until September 8 – to activate the nudity-blocking safeguards and vowed to change the law to force them to if they didn’t.
The September 8 deadline is today, but Apple and Google have not announced new measures in line with the demands.
![British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer departs 10 Downing Street for the House of Commons to attend the Prime Minister's Questions (PMQs) in London, United Kingdom on June 24, 2026. (Photo: Wiktor Szymanowicz/Future Publishing via Getty Images)](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_302683802-db2d.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
The NSPCC’s CEO, Chris Sherwood, said: ‘Children can’t continue to bear the brunt of tech companies’ inaction and excuses.
‘Apple and Google needed to urgently introduce these protections to ensure online sexual abuse is disrupted and prevented on children’s devices.
‘Now the deadline is up, the government must crack down and legislate. Only they can compel services to make these vital changes that children so desperately need.’
Google’s Sensitive Content Warnings blur sensitive imagery in Google Messages for supervised users and signed-in unsupervised teens, but the feature covers images only, not video.
Apple has introduced age checks for iPhone users, which activate safety features by default for those who are not verified as over 18.
However, nudity detection is not applied to the camera or broader apps, meaning children can still take, view, share and save nude images.
Campaigners and the government say this is not enough and want nudity across the whole device to be blocked by default, so it can only be deactivated via age assurance.
‘Social media platforms cannot be let off the hook’
![FILE PHOTO: Logo of an Apple store is seen as Apple Inc. reports fourth quarter earnings in Washington, U.S., January 27, 2022. REUTERS/Joshua Roberts/File Photo](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_234185282-f18a.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Anna Sabine MP, Liberal Democrat Spokesperson for Culture, Media and Sport, said: ‘Burnham needs to grow a backbone and stand up to the Silicon Valley tech bosses profiting off this awful content.
‘Social media platforms cannot be let off the hook – they must be truly held to account to protect children online.
‘The government should immediately bring forward emergency legislation to force platforms to introduce new safety protocols or face business disruption measures.’
The NSPCC has also revealed the top five platforms children mentioned in Childline counselling sessions, where they also spoke about their experience of online sexual abuse.
Between April 2025 and March 2026, Snapchat was mentioned in 324 counselling sessions where a young person also spoke about their experience of online sexual abuse, which was a 19% increase on the previous year.
TikTok was mentioned 234 times in similar conversations, followed by Instagram, with 197 mentions.
The messaging service Discord was mentioned 92 times, while WhatsApp came up 39 times.
The NSPCC has said that online sexual abuse has been the most commonly discussed concern in Childline counselling, where Snapchat and Instagram were mentioned over the past three years.
The charity has stressed that this data comes from word search data of notes from Childline sessions and that while the main concerns are likely to focus on negative experiences, mentions of apps in these counselling sessions could also be neutral or positive.
![hands with the mobile phone on the street](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_206355563-e3ea.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Meta, which owns Instagram and WhatsApp, has developed more than 50 tools that it says provide teens with safe experiences.
This includes putting teens in private accounts and protections on who can directly message them.
Instagram Teen Accounts also have content controls, time limits, and automatically hide potentially offensive comments and message requests.
A Discord spokesperson said: ‘Discord is a communications platform built to connect people around playing games.
‘Our safety systems combine advanced technology and human-led investigations, alongside user reports to help identify accounts or spaces engaged in harmful activity.
‘We take a proactive approach to combatting bad actors who seek to abuse our service and continuously invest in improving our efforts. Discord requires all users to be at least 13 to use our platform and we believe nowhere is our safety work more important than when it comes to teen users.
- 
	![PICTURED: Arthur Lundeen, 67 16107451 American Airlines passenger from hell DUCT-TAPED to seat on flight forced to divert over his terrifying racist and homophobic tirade](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_310814579-6ed9-e1788713390757.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=87px%2C129px%2C777px%2C438px&resize=646%2C363)
- Influencer, 43, dies after penis enlargement surgery in Thailand goes wrong
- 'I was assaulted at Reform's conference - the party celebrates attacks on women'
- Three-month-old girl dies while 'camping with family' in woodland
‘We’ve built a suite of protections for teen users that are now the default experience for all UK users, including sensitive content filters, safety alerts on unfamiliar senders, limited visibility to content of message requests, and enhanced privacy settings. We also provide teen users and their parents and guardians with important privacy and safety tools, including Teen Safety Assist and our Family Center.’
A Home Office spokesperson said: ‘We are committed to making it impossible for anyone under 18 to take, receive, view or send nude images on their mobile phones and tablets as part of our pledge to halve violence against women and girls.
’We are working closely with both Apple and Google to make this happen. We are clear that if they do not act, we will legislate to protect our children from predators who seek to exploit them online.’
Apple, Google, Meta, and TikTok were contacted for comment.
Get in touch with our news team by emailing us at webnews@metro.co.uk.
For more stories like this, check our news page.
summary: The NSPCC has warned that Childline counselling sessions regarding financially motivated sextortion involving children have more than doubled in a year, rising to 242 cases. Criminals are targeting young people—frequently teenage boys—by threatening to release naked images unless paid ransoms ranging from £20 to £3,000. This surge coincides with the expiration of a government deadline for tech giants like Apple and Google to implement device-level nudity-blocking technology, prompting calls for emergency legislation.
key_points: Childline recorded 242 cases of financially motivated sextortion between April 2025 and March 2026, more than double the previous year.
A large proportion of victims are male adolescents aged 14 to 17 who are targeted with fake profiles and threatened with the release of naked images.
A government deadline for Apple and Google to voluntarily implement device-level nudity-blocking technology on smartphones and tablets has expired without new blocking measures announced.
The NSPCC and various politicians are calling on the government to pass legislation forcing tech companies to introduce mandatory safety protocols.
Platforms such as Snapchat, TikTok, Instagram, Discord, and WhatsApp were mentioned by children in counselling sessions related to online sexual abuse.

title: GTA 6's Worldwide Release Times Revealed - with New Zealand Set to Receive Access 19 Hours Before Mexico and Central America
author: Digital Foundry; William Judd
content:
![GTA 6's Worldwide Release Times Revealed - with New Zealand Set to Receive Access 19 Hours Before Mexico and Central America 1](https://images.digitalfoundry.net/9397aeca1e9c7/gta-6s-worldwide-release-times-revealed-with-new-zealand-set-to-receive-access-19-hours-before-mexico-and-central-america-1.970x.jpg)
GTA 6 is coming out on November 19th this year, but when exactly on November 19th? The answer depends on where you are.
That's the chief finding from GTA fan site GTAVice.net, who evaluated regional PlayStation Store data to find out the exact release times for 15 different regions of the world, which can vary by up to 19 hours.
As you might have guessed from previous staggered releases, territories on the left side of the international date line will be the first to experience GTA 6, with New Zealand being first up. Kiwis get the game on 11:00 UTC on November 18th.
Meanwhile, Mexico, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico and Nicaragua get the game some 19 hours later, at 06:00 UTC on November 19th.
In terms of Digital Foundry team members, it looks like John and Alex will be the first to unlock the game at 23:00 UTC on November 18th, or midnight CET, with myself, Rich and Tom following one hour later when the clock hits midnight in the UK (00:00 UTC). Oliver, on the left side of Canada, gets the game five hours later than that, at 05:00 UTC on November 19th.
If you want to play the game early, you'll want to be on Xbox, as it's relatively straightforward to temporarily join the New Zealand time zone to unlock ahead of time via Settings - whereas on PlayStation, this requires a whole new account that has to purchase the game with a local payment method.
Are you planning to play GTA 6 the instant it unlocks? Or are you going to get to it whenever you'd next normally play games? Let me know in the comments below.
summary: Regional PlayStation Store data analyzed by GTAVice.net reveals that GTA 6 will have staggered worldwide release times on November 19, varying by up to 19 hours depending on the territory. New Zealand will receive access first at 11:00 UTC on November 18, while Mexico and Central America will gain access 19 hours later at 06:00 UTC on November 19. Players can potentially access the game early by using an Xbox to temporarily change their time zone to New Zealand, whereas PlayStation users must create a separate local account.
key_points: GTA 6 release times vary globally by up to 19 hours based on regional PlayStation Store data.
New Zealand gets access first at 11:00 UTC on November 18.
Mexico and Central America receive the game 19 hours after New Zealand at 06:00 UTC on November 19.
Xbox users can easily unlock the game early by switching their time zone to New Zealand, unlike PlayStation users who need a local account.

title: Tim Cook Won't Appear in Apple's September 9 Event Video
author: Tim Hardwick
content:
![Tim Cook Executive Chair 16x9 1](https://images.macrumors.com/t/vnHsyqFM4iFhsdeJozSAnqEXsnQ=/400x0/article-new/2026/09/Tim-Cook-Executive-Chair-16x9-1.jpg?lossy) Tim Cook will attend the screening for Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event this Wednesday, but he will not feature in the event video itself, according to sources cited by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Cook stepped down as Apple CEO on September 1 to become executive chairman of the company, paving the way for John Ternus to take over the top job.
In his latest Power On newsletter, Gurman said that Apple has "carefully orchestrated this transition to make Ternus the face of the foldable iPhone and all the new products to come. Putting Cook in the presentation would just undermine that."
summary: Apple's upcoming September 9 event video will not feature Tim Cook, who recently transitioned from CEO to executive chairman. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the decision is part of an orchestrated transition to establish new CEO John Ternus as the face of upcoming products like the foldable iPhone. Cook will still attend the event's screening.
key_points: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO on September 1 to become executive chairman.
John Ternus has taken over as Apple's CEO.
Cook will attend the September 9 'Surprise and Shine' event screening but will not appear in the video.
The omission is intended to establish Ternus as the face of the foldable iPhone and future products.

title: Sony brings back its fan-favorite headphones, the XM4
author: John Higgins
content:
Six years ago Sony and Bose were in the middle of a noise-canceling battle, with each new model of headphones better than the last. In the fall of 2020, Sony released the WH-1000XM4 headphones to wide acclaim. They sat atop best headphones lists for years, thanks to their great sound, competitive ANC, and compact size, until they went out of stock. Now Sony has brought them back, with minor improvements, as the WH-1000XM4C.
Six years later, Sony revisits its legendary XM4 headphones
After the WH-1000XM4 were discontinued in 2025, Sony is bringing them back as the WH-1000XM4C.
![sony-wh-1000xm4c-headphones-comparison](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sony-wh-1000xm4c-headphones-comparison.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
![sony-wh-1000xm4c-headphones-comparison](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sony-wh-1000xm4c-headphones-comparison.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
The XM4C look identical to the original XM4 (although they now have a lavender option), with the same hinge design and ability to fold up. It’s a compact design that Sony moved away from when it released the XM5 in 2022, and then returned to (although not quite as compact) with the XM6. But it’s not just the look that’s returned. The XM4C still use the same QN1 processing chip and four microphones for ANC. That design is showing its age: The XM5 still used the QN1, but had eight mics. Last year’s XM6 have 12, plus the new QN3 chip.
![A person in a gray sweatshirt wearing lavender Sony WH-1000XM4C headphones.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Sony-WH-1000XM4C-Lavender-Lifestyle.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
Sony did update the XM4C’s sound profile to bring it in line with current models, and the headphones have a 10-band EQ in the Headphones app, instead of the 5-band on the XM4, plus a gaming preset. The XM4C also support Bluetooth 6 instead of 5. Surprisingly, the battery performance on the new headphones is slightly worse. Sony claims the XM4C get up to 27 hours of use with ANC on as opposed to 30 hours previously. Not a huge difference, and still more than enough for a cross-country trip.
The XM4C will be available later this fall for $300, which is $50 cheaper than the XM4 when they first came out (and $100 cheaper than the XM6 are now), but more than they could be found for before being discontinued.
I have loved the Sony XM4 since they came out, and still have my pair hanging on the side of my desk. Beyond nostalgia, though, I’m confused why they’re coming back. A review sample of the XM4C arrived at my door while I was writing this, so some deeper investigation will be coming soon. But the headphones industry has moved forward in the past six years, and I’m not sure there’s a need to go back. And the XM5, while they don’t fold up as nicely as the XM4C, are excellent headphones and currently available for $200 (though that price may be an effort to clear out inventory ahead of the XM4C).
Alongside the XM4C, Sony released the next generation of two of its less-expensive midrange and entry-level headphone lines: the WH-CH730N and WH-CH530. They both get the same 10-band EQ upgrade and gaming EQ preset as the XM4C, and the CH730N will now fold up into a more compact form.
![Green Sony WH-CH530 headphones resting against some books on a bench.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Sony-WH-CH530-Mint-lifestyle.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0.083333333333336%2C0%2C99.833333333333%2C100&w=2400)
![A person wearing the blue Sony WH-CH730N headphones.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Sony-WH-CH730N-Blue-Lifestyle.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0.041666666666664%2C0%2C99.916666666667%2C100&w=2400)
The two headphones also get a boost to battery life according to Sony: The CH730N get up to 50 hours with ANC, and the CH530 get up to 55 hours (there’s no ANC on the CH530). A new safe mode in the app allows a user to limit the max volume output of the headphones. It’s a nice addition for parents looking to protect their kids’ hearing, although there’s no way to lock the limit once it’s been set.
The WH-CH530 come in black, cobalt, mint green, white, pink, and coral and cost $70. For $180, you can get the WH-CN730N in black, blue, oat, white, or pink. Both headphones are available now.
![Sony Hello Kitty headphones, case, and bag.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sony-hello-kitty-headphones.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
Sony is also doing a partnership with Hello Kitty. Bundles include headphones — the WH-1000XM6, WH-CH730N, or WH-CH530 available in black or pink — a Hello Kitty-shaped carrying pouch, and Hello Kitty-branded bag. The bundles will be available in limited supply later this year on the Sony website only.
summary: Sony is bringing back its popular WH-1000XM4 headphones as the updated WH-1000XM4C, featuring a new lavender color option, Bluetooth 6 support, and an updated sound profile with a 10-band EQ. The new model retains the compact, foldable design of the original XM4 and will be available this fall for $300. Alongside the XM4C, Sony has released the new WH-CH730N and WH-CH530 midrange and entry-level headphones, as well as limited-edition Hello Kitty bundles.
key_points: The WH-1000XM4C headphones return with minor improvements, including a lavender color option, Bluetooth 6 support, and a 10-band EQ.
Battery performance for the XM4C is slightly reduced compared to the original, offering up to 27 hours of use with ANC on.
The XM4C will be available later this fall priced at $300.
Sony also launched new midrange and entry-level models, the WH-CH730N and WH-CH530, featuring increased battery life and app-based volume limits.
Limited-edition Hello Kitty bundles featuring select headphone models, a shaped carrying pouch, and a branded bag will be available later this year.

title: Xiaomi 18 Fold: New colors officially revealed
author: Jacob Fisher
content:
Xiaomi has revealed two additional finishes for its upcoming 18 Fold, expanding the range beyond the previously showcased red model. The new options are Black and Warm Gold White (see images below), with the company presenting the former as a restrained, business-appropriate choice and the latter as a softer, more premium-looking alternative.
![](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/8/8/csm_096e4f6c-5e77-4e55-b6dd-807b492072cf_bfdbe0bb1a.jpg)
![](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/e/1/csm_5e04ce3a-e058-4ae2-abcf-9bf457002e2f_a8076f1de7.jpg)
As can be seen below, the 18 Fold uses a mid-fold design with a narrow, symmetrical hinge, rounded corners and a flat surrounding frame. According to ithome, the external- and internal displays will measure 5.38 inches and 7.58 inches, respectively, both utilizing Xiaomi’s Super Pixel technology and providing peak brightness of up to 4,000 nits. As for cameras, the foldable is said to have a Leica 200 MP main sensor on the rear, joined by a 50 MP 3.5x periscope telephoto and 50 MP ultra-wide camera.
![](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/8/5/csm_ef8936bf-c5ad-4d10-9d8e-ba6971ea2f91_7d21845afd.png)
Beyond its displays and cameras, the foldable is expected to debut the Xring O3 flagship chipset and LPDDR6 RAM for the first time and include a 6,000mAh battery, along with 67W wired and 50W wireless charging. However, prospective buyers outside China face a major limitation: the Xiaomi 18 Fold is set for Chinese-market availability only. Xiaomi is due to formally present the device on September 7.
summary: Xiaomi has officially revealed two new color finishes, Black and Warm Gold White, for its upcoming 18 Fold smartphone, joining the previously shown red model. Scheduled for a formal presentation on September 7, the device features a mid-fold design, advanced display and camera specifications, and is expected to be available exclusively in the Chinese market.
key_points: Xiaomi added Black and Warm Gold White finishes to the 18 Fold lineup alongside the previously showcased red model.
The device features a mid-fold design with a 5.38-inch external display and a 7.58-inch internal display, both reaching up to 4,000 nits peak brightness.
Camera specifications reportedly include a 200 MP Leica main sensor, a 50 MP periscope telephoto lens, and a 50 MP ultra-wide camera.
The foldable is expected to debut the Xring O3 flagship chipset and LPDDR6 RAM, paired with a 6,000mAh battery supporting 67W wired and 50W wireless charging.
The Xiaomi 18 Fold is planned for release exclusively in the Chinese market and will be formally presented on September 7.

title: Tiny cash buffers leave small UK TV firms at risk of going bust, analysis finds
author: Mark Sweney
content:
Hundreds of small UK TV companies have so little cash in reserve that a filming overrun or a delay to a series could send them bust, an industry body has warned, as programme budget cuts by broadcasters threaten their future.
Analysis of the Companies House accounts filings of more than 200 of the estimated 800 independent TV production companies in the UK by the industry body Indielab has found that 40% face running out of cash within the next two years.
The analysis of three years of filings made by small independent TV producers, the “indies” that make up 85% of the UK’s production sector, identified a dramatic drain on the financial reserves they use to weather tough trading periods.
The reserves of more than half declined over the three-year period, with 40% registering a decline of almost a third, while the financial cushion for 31% was slashed by more than half.
The analysis found that the amount held in reserves by a typical small indie – the median amount of the sample of 203 – was only £42,000 at the end of the three-year analysis period.
The comparable figure at the beginning of the period was £51,000, already a slim reserve fund to rely on to bridge funding shortages.
“[The £42,000] buffer would not cover the cost of a single delayed commission, a production overrun, or a series put on hold [by a broadcaster] after delivery,” said Victoria Powell, the chief executive of Indielab. “The picture is stark. Small producers are the most exposed part of the ecosystem. When commissioning spend falls, they feel it first and hardest. Our data shows the sector’s health is being eroded, year on year.”
A string of high-profile TV production companies have already been wound down in the past two years.
![Two male actors from Lost Boys & Fairies sit at a kitchen table with a door and shelving behind them and fruit in a bowl and other food on the table](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ae2fcbc0117f7fea4f22f30cded61502d5e093f2/427_0_3858_2857/master/3858.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
These include Euston Films, the maker of the pre-apocalyptic thriller Hard Sun and the train drama Nightsleeper for the BBC, and Dare Pictures, which has produced Channel 4 shows including Fugitive: The Mystery of the Crypto Queen and UK Prisons Exposed: Sex, Drugs & Corruption.
Other notable production closures include Leeds-based Duck Soup Films, which made the drama Lost Boys & Fairies for the BBC and Channel 4’s Dreamers, and the factual producer Proper Content, which had credits including the BBC documentary P Diddy: The Rise and Fall, the Channel 5 royal docuseries The King’s Guard and the Channel 4 show The School That Tried To End Racism.
“We have seen many notable closures across the sector in the last two years,” Powell said. “We know of many more companies that have quietly closed or mothballed outside the headlines. Our data strongly suggests this trend will accelerate.”
Last week, Everyone TV, the joint venture owned by the BBC, ITV, Channel 4 and Channel 5, released a report that warned of a “spiral of decline” affecting the production industry if broadcaster budgets continued to be cut.
Despite the arrival of the deep-pocketed US streamers such as Netflix, Amazon and Disney+, the UK production industry still relies heavily on traditional UK broadcasters for their livelihood.
after newsletter promotion
The report, by Oliver & Ohlbaum, found that public service broadcasters (PSBs) remain the leading source of UK original commissions and production for small indies, accounting for 71% of UK original content investment in 2024 and 85% of all original hours last year.
However, the total amount spent on commissioning programmes by all UK-based broadcasters has fallen from £1.99bn in 2022 to £1.73bn in 2024 – the lowest level since the industry shut down during the Covid pandemic in 2020 – according to the most recent figures from the industry body Pact.
This fall has mainly been because of significant decreases by multichannel broadcasters, such as Sky, where spend has declined by almost 40% over that period.
Figures from the British Film Institute showed that spending on prestige shows – high-end TV costing at least £1m an hour to make – by domestic broadcasters has declined from £794m in 2023 to £688m last year.
“PSBs with a statutory duty to support independent production need to consider what that duty really means in practice, and whether they are currently meeting it,” Powell said. “The accounts of 203 indie TV companies should be a wake-up call to the sector.”
Indielab’s research focused on small indies with a turnover of less than £10m.
Pact, which represents the wider industry, says it has 800 independent production company members, the majority of which are small and medium-sized with a turnover of less than £50m.
summary: An analysis by the industry body Indielab reveals that 40% of small UK independent TV production companies face running out of cash within the next two years. With a typical median cash reserve of only £42,000, these firms lack the financial cushion to survive filming overruns, delayed commissions, or broadcaster budget cuts. This precarious financial state is exacerbated by a drop in total commissioning spend by UK-based broadcasters, which has fallen from £1.99bn in 2022 to £1.73bn in 2024.
key_points: About 40% of small independent UK TV production companies face running out of cash within two years.
The median cash reserve for a typical small indie dropped from £51,000 to £42,000 over a three-year period.
Total spending on commissioning programmes by UK broadcasters fell from £1.99bn in 2022 to £1.73bn in 2024.
Several high-profile production companies, including Euston Films, Dare Pictures, Duck Soup Films, and Proper Content, have wound down in the past two years.

title: Here's how iPhone Ultra's form factor could compare to other Apple products - 9to5Mac
author: Michael Burkhardt
content:
![](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/03/iphone-fold-mockup-red.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
This month, Apple will be unveiling its first foldable iPhone – rumored to be called iPhone Ultra. It’s going to feature a 5.5-inch outer display and 7.6-inch inner display. In July, Samsung introduced the new Galaxy Z Fold 8 – and it comes with those same screen sizes.
Whether or not you believe Samsung only made this phone to preempt the iPhone Ultra is a different story – but one way or another, seeing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 gives us a great early idea of what iPhone Ultra will feel like in the real world.
Reviewers who have early access to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 have posted plenty of comparison photos of it and other devices on Twitter. Since the iPhone Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold 8 are going to be dimensionally similar, this serves as a great representation of how iPhone Ultra will look and feel in the real world.
Ray Wong posted multiple comparisons of Galazy Z Fold 8, against the previous generation iPad mini, highlighting that you’re truly getting an iPad mini-like display in your pocket – just without the chunkier bezels.
Meanwhile, enthusiast Shishir shared photos comparing the iPhone 13 mini to the Galaxy Z Fold 8. The iPhone 13 mini is slightly taller than the foldable, though it is similarly small. For those who mourn the loss of iPhone mini, iPhone Ultra could get you pretty close.
Personally, seeing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 last week made me more excited for the iPhone Ultra than ever. The two should be nearly identical in terms of physical form factor (though iPhone Ultra will have curved corners) – so it may truly be our best idea of what Apple has in store before we get to see it in September.
